The patch fixes a NameError typo (cotm -> cothm) in hyperbolic.py, which resolves the issue. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess risk; the extra reproduce_error.py script is harmless but unneeded.

The patch applies the slice to the whole prefetch queryset, so the LIMIT applies globally rather than per parent instance. A prefetch of [:3] across many categories would return only 3 rows total, giving wrong results (the real fix uses window functions to slice per parent). It also hacks `_restore_slice` as an attribute on the queryset, which is fragile, and leaves a stray reproduce script in the repo. It only touches reverse FK and reverse one-to-one, not M2M, and `_restore_slice` is set on the original queryset, mutating it. The hidden tests would fail.

The visible part of the patch only adds get-pip.py, a ~24k-line vendored pip bootstrap script, to the repo root. It contains no change to _pytest/mark/structures.py or any other pytest code, so it does not make get_unpacked_marks consider the MRO, and the issue stays unresolved. The patch is truncated, so a real fix could be hidden in the remainder, but a stray get-pip.py is itself an unwanted artifact that should not be merged.
The patch fixes a simple typo (cotm -> cothm) that caused a NameError. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval risk, and it correctly resolves the issue.

The patch iterates over obj.__class__.__mro__, but get_unpacked_marks is called with the class itself (e.g. a Class node's obj) or a function, so obj.__class__ is the metaclass `type` (or function), not the class's MRO. For a class, obj.__class__.__mro__ is (type, object), which has no pytestmark, so marks on classes are lost entirely. The upstream fix uses `obj.__mro__` when obj is a class, falling back to getattr otherwise. This patch breaks existing behaviour, including function marks stored on the function itself.

The patch raises ValueError for sliced querysets in ForwardManyToOneDescriptor, which is the opposite of what the issue asks for. The real fix uses window functions to apply the slice per parent instance in prefetch_one_level, and this patch does not implement that. Hidden tests that prefetch sliced querysets would still fail, and it adds a new exception to existing code paths.

The patch fixes a simple typo (cotm -> cothm) in a variable name; it introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval concerns, and it resolves the NameError from the issue.

The patch commits binary artifacts (output*.png) and a reproduce_error.py script to the repo root. It also parses the offset string by string replacement, which is fragile: matplotlib's offset can look like '1e6' or '+1.5e3' or use mathtext. Appending the offset to only the last label is a hack that gives misleading output. ScalarFormatter may not be imported. The trailing whitespace and duplicated format_ticks calls add smell. The upstream fix just uses formatter.get_offset() and appends it to the legend title.

The patch makes element_id optional in django.utils.html.json_script, emitting the id attribute only when provided. However, the template filter django.template.defaultfilters.json_script still requires element_id, so the issue's use-case (using it from templates) is not resolved. The upstream fix changed the filter to accept an optional argument (element_id=None) too, and hidden tests likely test `{{ value|json_script }}` in the template filter tests. Without that change, the filter call without an argument raises TypeError.

The patch returns self.args[1] (the set) from Contains.as_set, an O(1) change with no performance concerns. Upstream sympy's fix is the same, so it should resolve the issue and have no scalability impact.

The patch makes element_id optional in both the utility and the template filter, and omits the id attribute when it is None. The upstream fix uses `if element_id:` in the same way, so behavior matches. In templates, `{{ value|json_script }}` without an argument fails at the filter level, but a filter with a default argument is valid, so it works.

This closely matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #26780): a window RowNumber partitioned by the relation field filters sliced prefetch querysets in a single query. Performance is as intended, with no N+1 queries or leaks; the extra get_compiler call to read the ordering is a minor one-time cost per prefetch. Filtering on a window expression is supported in this Django version.

This matches the upstream pytest fix (PR #10356): get_unpacked_marks walks the MRO for classes, and store_mark uses consider_mro=False so a subclass doesn't copy base marks. Upstream also added a metaclass-compatible variant, but the core logic here is equivalent. The upstream version of this patch is essentially identical, including the __dict__ lookup. One side effect: a class whose pytestmark is set via a metaclass property would not appear in __dict__, but that matches upstream behaviour. Hidden tests should pass.

The patch is small and clear, with explanatory comments, and the hasattr guards are reasonable since formatters can vary. The duplication across scales.py and utils.py is minor. Mutating a user-supplied formatter in place is a slight smell, but the style is consistent with the surrounding code.

The core fix in _arithmetic_mask matches the upstream astropy fix: when operand.mask is None, return a deepcopy of self.mask. It also handles the self.mask None case and the collapse case. However, the patch pins setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml, which is an unrelated build change that could break builds, and it adds a stray reproduction script to the repo root. These are not likely to affect hidden tests, but they are unwanted changes. The logic fix is correct.
The patch changes as_set to return self.args[1], an O(1) operation with no extra work, allocation, or scalability concerns. It matches the upstream fix, and there are no performance defects.

The change wraps the first object's attrs in dict() so the merged result gets a shallow copy instead of a reference to the source attrs. It introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess issues. The fix matches the issue's suggestion and the upstream approach.

The change to `dict(variable_attrs[0])` is the fix the issue itself proposes, and it introduces no security risk: no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal or subprocess use. The added reproduce.py is a harmless script. Functionally it fixes the shallow aliasing on the top-level attrs dict, though nested mutable values would still be shared (upstream used a plain dict() copy too).

The upstream fix (seaborn PR) makes legend labels incorporate the offset, but it does so via `formatter.get_offset()` and a different approach: it uses `axis.major.formatter.format_ticks(locs)` followed by `if hasattr(formatter, 'set_useOffset'): formatter.set_useOffset(False)` and `set_scientific(False)`. This patch instead appends the offset text to every label, e.g. '3.5 (1e6)', which is cluttered and semantically confusing, and the hidden tests likely expect labels with the full numbers (e.g. '3,000,000'-style) rather than annotated labels. Style-wise the change is small and readable, but the output format is a questionable design choice and does not match the expected behavior.

The patch changes the mask setter to coerce every mask to bool, which does not touch the arithmetic code in NDArithmeticMixin where the bug lives. Converting masks to bool also breaks bitwise flag masks like 64 and 8, which the issue's example relies on, and it would break existing tests that check mask dtype and values. The mask * no-mask case still reaches np.bitwise_or with None, so the TypeError remains. The diff also adds or removes a trailing newline, which is cosmetic.

The patch leaves a stray reproduce_error.py in the repo root, which is clutter that shouldn't be merged. The FeatureUnion change (union and reindex of indices) alters behavior and is unnecessary; it could introduce NaNs or reorder rows, and it is not the upstream fix, which skips setting the index. The silent index drop in _wrap_in_pandas_container hides mismatches without documentation, and there is no test.

The patch makes element_id optional in utils.html.json_script. It builds the id attribute via nested format_html, which returns a SafeString, so the outer format_html does not double-escape it. With no id, '' is inserted and the output is '<script type="application/json">...</script>'. This matches upstream behavior. However, the template filter json_script in django/template/defaultfilters.py still requires the argument. The upstream fix also changed the filter to `def json_script(value, element_id=None)`. The issue is about the utility, and hidden tests likely cover both utils and the filter; the filter test with no argument (`{{ value|json_script }}`) may exist upstream. Upstream commit 'Fixed #31639? ' ... in Django 4.1, the filter was changed too, and tests include test_json_script_without_id in both template filter tests and utils tests. Since the filter is not updated, the filter test would fail with a missing argument TypeError.

The patch makes Contains.as_set return self.args[1], which is semantically wrong: Contains(x, S) as a set is the set of x values satisfying it, which is S only when x is a bare symbol. For Contains(x+1, S) or Contains(x, S) with multiple free symbols, this gives wrong results. The upstream fix raises NotImplementedError for non-symbol args and returns the set when the first arg is a Symbol. Hidden tests likely check that Contains(x, Reals).as_set() equals Reals, which would pass, and possibly that non-symbol cases raise NotImplementedError, which would fail. Performance-wise there are no issues; the work is O(1). The stray reproduce.py and test_edge_cases.py files at the repo root are clutter but harmless to tests, and test_edge_cases would not be collected by pytest unless the file is picked up and its module-level code runs. It could be collected, since the name matches test_*.py, and it runs at import, calling EmptySet(), which is not callable, so it would raise a collection error. That could break a full test run but not the hidden tests specifically. Perf focus: nothing significant.

The change wraps the first attrs mapping in dict() so the merged result gets a shallow copy. It adds no injection, deserialization, secret, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess exposure, so there is no security concern.

The patch compiles the regex with IGNORECASE and handles lowercase 'no' in data values, which matches the upstream fix. The regex is compiled once per call, as before, so there is no performance regression, and I see no algorithmic or resource concerns.

The regex gets an inline (?i) flag at the start, which is valid in Python and has no performance cost. However, the rest of the QDP parser may still be case-sensitive: _get_tables_from_qdp_file uses command_lines.lower().split() and checks 'NO' values. In the upstream fix, re.compile(_type_re, re.IGNORECASE) was used and 'NO' handling was left as is. The (?i) at the start of the pattern is concatenated into _type_re as part of a larger pattern, e.g. rf'^\s*((?P<command>{_command_re})|...)', so it would no longer sit at the start of the combined pattern. Python 3.11+ raises an error for global flags not at the start of the expression, and earlier versions emit a DeprecationWarning, which pytest may turn into an error. That is a real failure risk. The unrelated pyproject.toml change and the stray test file are also noise.

The change adds a trivial length check in a lambda, so there is no performance impact. It resolves the IndexError for scalar x. The scratch files (reproduce script, edge-case test) are clutter but not a performance issue. The upstream fix is the same: `attrs[1] if len(attrs) > 1 else {}`. Hidden tests should pass.

Scoped inline flag `(?i:...)` is supported in Python 3.6+, so the regex compiles. Performance is unchanged, since the regex is only compiled once per call, as before. However, the patch only changes the command regex in _line_type. Downstream, _get_tables_from_qdp_file does `command = line.strip().split()` then checks `command[1].lower() == 'serr'`; if the original code uses `.lower()` it works, and the upstream fix only changed the regex plus the compile flag. The upstream fix was `_command_re = r"READ [TS]ERR(\s+[0-9]+)+"` with `re.IGNORECASE` in the compile. The existing code compares `command[1].lower()`, so it is fine. There are no performance concerns.

The patch adds an optional rhs parameter to KeyTransform.as_mysql/as_oracle/as_sqlite, but nothing calls these with rhs. The existing In lookup still compiles lhs via compiler.compile(self.lhs), which calls as_vendor(compiler, connection) without rhs, so behavior is unchanged. No KeyTransformIn lookup is registered, and the issue's __in on key transforms is not fixed. The upstream fix added a KeyTransformIn class that handles JSON-encoding of the rhs values, and this patch has nothing like it.

The patch removes the index reassignment for DataFrame inputs and updates the docstring to say the index is ignored in that case. This matches the upstream scikit-learn fix, and the change is minimal and clear. The docstring accurately describes the new behavior, so there are no maintainability or style concerns.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #31936) for KeyTransformIn. It handles Oracle with JSON_QUERY/JSON_VALUE, MariaDB with JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT), and SQLite/MySQL with JSON_EXTRACT. The upstream code is essentially identical, and the registration is placed correctly.

The patch adds a length guard that avoids the crash for DataFrame outputs, but the issue's transformer returns a Series, so the guard may not be reached. The upstream fix changed FeatureUnion to handle the index in _hstack and the wrapping logic. This patch also adds a stray blank line at the top of the file and silently skips index assignment with no comment, which is poor style. The Series case would go to pd.DataFrame(data_to_wrap, index=index, ...), which for a Series with a mismatched index reindexes and produces NaNs or wrong data rather than raising an error. The result is likely incorrect, and the patch is not robust.

The change only forces lazy strings to str before concatenation in the add filter, using hasattr on a private proxy attribute. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval risk. The stray reproduce_issue.py is a harmless repo-clutter script with no security impact.

The core fix (setting self.data.cols and calling _set_col_formats) mirrors the upstream fix and adds only negligible work, so there is no performance problem. However, the patch also pins setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml and adds a stray reproduce.py, which are unrelated changes. The pyproject pin could break the build in some environments.

The lambda returns getattr(x, "attrs", {}) when keep_attrs is True, which fixes the IndexError for scalar x. This is O(1) per call with no meaningful performance cost, no leaks, and no scaling issues. The upstream fix is essentially identical.

The visit_Tuple change correctly emits a trailing comma for single-element tuples and leaves empty and multi-element tuples unchanged, which fixes the issue. The patch also adds stray files and pins dependency versions in setup.py, but these don't affect the functional behavior of the fix or the hidden tests.

The core change in UserCreationForm.save matches the upstream Django fix: it calls self.save_m2m() after user.save() when commit=True. The extra files (reproduce_issue.py, test_fix.py) are stray scripts in the repo root, which is clutter but should not affect hidden tests, since they are not collected as tests and are not named test_*.py in a tests directory. Hmm, test_fix.py sits in the root and could be collected only if the runner targets it, which Django's runtests does not do. The docstring also has trailing whitespace, which is only cosmetic.

In UserCreationForm.save, super().save(commit=False) sets self.save_m2m on the ModelForm, so when commit=True the patch calls it after user.save(). The hasattr guard is harmless, and the actual Django fix is `self._save_m2m()` after `user.save()`. With commit=False, the caller still gets save_m2m as before. Behavior matches the upstream fix and resolves the issue.

The patch commits a stray reproduce_squash_issue.py script at the repo root, which is clutter that should not be merged. The loader change also does not fix the issue: the real fix is in MigrationExecutor.unapply_migration, which should record only the replaced migrations as unapplied rather than the squash migration. The loader change alters semantics in a confusing way and leaves a dangling comment without a period.

The patch's KeyTransformIn is likely broken. The upstream fix subclasses lookups.In and uses the JSONField's process_rhs with JSON_EXTRACT/JSON_QUOTE handling. This patch's get_prep_lookup calls get_prep_value on the lhs output_field, which for a KeyTransform is a JSONField, so it json.dumps each value. That turns 0 into the string '0'. On SQLite the SQL then wraps each value as JSON_EXTRACT(JSON(%s), '$'); for a numeric 0 this may work, but for string values the dumped '"a"' parses to a string and may match. The MySQL branch uses CAST(%s AS JSON), which is plausible. The Oracle branch builds JSON_VALUE(%s, '$.%%s') and passes json_path as a param, but compile_json_path already returns '$.key', giving '$.$.key' inside quotes, so it is wrong. The rhs params are also taken from self.rhs rather than the processed rhs. The first param order is also wrong because lhs_params are ignored, and when the lhs is not a KeyTransform the code falls through only for non-KeyTransform lhs. It also adds stray files (reproduce.py, test_app). The Oracle path is broken, and the rest is fragile. Also, in the SQLite branch, the JSON(%s) param for a string like 'a' dumped to '"a"' works, but for booleans and None it differs, and an empty rhs generates invalid SQL 'IN ()'. Overall the patch is likely to fail the hidden tests.

The patch adds save_m2m() under commit=True, which fixes the issue, but it keeps the original `if commit: user.save()` and adds a second `if commit:` block that calls user.save() again. This saves the user twice, which is redundant and can fire extra signals (pre_save/post_save), so tests counting signals or queries may fail. The upstream fix is a single save followed by save_m2m(). The duplicate save is a real regression and sloppy.

The patch coerces both operands to str in the add filter fallback. This introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess risks. It does change behaviour for lists (e.g. [1]+[2] now yields '[1][2]' instead of a concatenated list), which would likely break existing tests, but that is a correctness concern outside my security focus.

The patch special-cases a single-element tuple to render as "(1,)" and leaves multi-element and empty tuples unchanged, which matches the issue. The visit_Tuple method is the only place tuples are unparsed, so no other code path is affected.
The patch correctly renders a 1-element tuple with a trailing comma, keeps the empty tuple as "()", and leaves multi-element tuples unchanged. It matches the upstream fix.

The patch adds __add__ and __radd__ to the lazy proxy, delegating to the cast result. This is plain operator delegation with no injection, deserialization, secrets, path, or subprocess exposure. It matches the upstream Django fix, so there is no security concern.

The change adds a constant-time length check in the keep_attrs lambda, with no complexity, resource, or scalability impact. Behaviorally, when x is a scalar only cond's attrs remain, so it falls back to attrs[0]. The upstream fix used `getattr(x, "attrs", {})`, which keeps nothing from cond, so this could differ: tests may expect result attrs to be empty, whereas here the result would carry cond's attrs. The issue's example has `xr.DataArray([1,2,3]) > 0` with no attrs, so it would pass. The hidden test, test_where_attrs, checks cond with attrs {"attr": "cond"}, x scalar 1, y scalar 0, and expects attrs {}. With this patch the result would get cond's attrs {"attr": "cond"}, so that test would likely fail. Even so, the performance angle is fine.

The mode property is a cheap string replace with no algorithmic, resource, or scalability cost, and it fixes the issue. The stray reproduce.py file is clutter, not a performance concern. Upstream does the same thing (`return self.buffer.mode.replace('b', '')`).

The patch adds self.data.cols and calls _set_col_formats() once before writing, matching the upstream fix. This is O(columns) setup work with no new loops, leaks, or scalability concerns. The existing per-column str_vals call in the writer picks up the formats.

The patch fixes the bug, but the control flow is now redundant: the squashed migration's record_unapplied call is duplicated in both the if and else branches. It would be cleaner to loop over replaces if present and then unconditionally record the migration itself. The upstream fix did exactly this. The duplication is a minor style smell, though the behavior is correct and the comment is clear.

The patch sets col.info.format on the table's columns from self.data.formats, which mutates the caller's table (or a shallow copy) as a side effect. Also, it's unclear whether the table is copied before this point; the writer typically copies the table in write(), but in HTML.write the table is passed directly. The upstream fix computed formatted values via self.data._set_col_formats() and col.info.format. A col.info.format that is a callable works for str_vals in the Column formatting. Performance-wise it's O(columns) and negligible. The mutation could leak into the user's table, but that is a correctness concern rather than performance, and the data object's formats are probably applied to a copy anyway. The trailing-newline diff is harmless.

The patch removes the final e-step and returns argmax of _estimate_weighted_log_prob(X) after _set_parameters(best_params), which is exactly what predict() computes (predict uses _estimate_weighted_log_prob(X).argmax(axis=1)). So fit_predict and predict now agree for any n_init. The leftover best_log_resp variable is unused but harmless. The stray reproduce script is untidy but doesn't break tests. Argmax of the weighted log prob is the same as argmax of log_resp since the normalization is constant per sample. Existing tests should pass; the upstream fix did a final e-step after setting best params, equivalent here.

The patch removes the else branch so the squashed migration itself is always recorded as unapplied, in addition to the replaced ones. This matches the upstream Django fix. The code is simple and the updated comment is clear.

The patch adds a `mode` property to EncodedFile that strips 'b' from the underlying buffer's mode, which matches the upstream fix. The cost is a single string replace per access, with no leaks or scalability concerns.

The patch removes 'b' from the mode before os.fdopen(newfd, mode, 0). In Python 3, unbuffered (buffering=0) is only allowed in binary mode, so os.fdopen with a text mode and buffering 0 raises ValueError: can't have unbuffered text I/O. This would break capture for every FDCapture. The upstream fix keeps the binary file and overrides EncodedFile.mode to strip 'b'. As written, the patch breaks existing behaviour.

The linkcheck change is a simple, correct exception-clause extension with no injection, deserialization, or secrets risk. The setup.py dependency pins and the stray reproduce script are unrelated clutter and not security vulnerabilities (the pins are restrictive version caps, not insecure sources).

The patch moves the final e-step to after the best parameters are restored with _set_parameters, so fit_predict labels match predict for n_init>1. This matches the upstream scikit-learn fix, and the warning logic is unaffected.

The patch matches the upstream fix (catching ValueError alongside TypeError) and resolves the empty-items case. It adds no new work, so there is no performance regression; the existing list-building in max() is unchanged.

The patch only adds TooManyRedirects to the except clause so the GET fallback runs. It introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal or exec risk. The second change is redundant, since TooManyRedirects is already an Exception subclass, but it is harmless. It assumes `requests` is imported in that module, and that is not a security matter.

The functional fix is plausible, but the patch commits stray scratch files (reproduce_issue.py, test_app.py) to the repo root, which is a clear maintainability problem. It also adds a function-local import inside as_sql and special-cases ExtractIsoYear with isinstance in the generic YearLookup, whereas upstream fix unregisters the optimized lookups for iso_year. No tests were added.

Using max(..., default=None) handles the empty items case without raising ValueError and matches the upstream Django fix. The list comprehension is unchanged, so there is no new performance cost or resource issue.

The patch sets the model to best_params before the final e-step, so fit_predict labels come from the same parameters that predict uses. The upstream fix moved the final e-step after the parameter setting in the same way. Here best_params is defined in the loop, and _set_parameters is called later after the warning check, which is harmless. Setting parameters twice is idempotent. This fixes the n_init>1 inconsistency. The one subtle point is the case max_iter=0 or similar, where best_params may be None. With n_init>=1 and max_iter>=1, best_params is set whenever lower_bound > max_lower_bound, and max_lower_bound starts at -inf, so it is always set. If lower_bound were NaN, best_params could stay None, but that is an edge case that the original code also handles by calling _set_parameters(best_params) later.

The upstream fix adds `__str__` to the `Choices` base class so it covers IntegerChoices too, returning str(self.value). This patch adds `__str__` only to TextChoices, so IntegerChoices still stringifies as 'MyChoice.FIRST', and the hidden tests likely check `str(Foo.A)` for IntegerChoices as well. The field-level changes do not fix this. Behaviour for `str(IntegerChoices.member)` stays as before and the upstream tests (e.g. test_str in ChoicesTests for Suit, Vehicle) would fail. The patch also leaves a stray reproduce.py in the repo.

The patch only widens an except clause to also catch TooManyRedirects and retry with GET, using the same URL and the same request settings. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess risk.

The template change `'%(function)s(%(distinct)s %(expressions)s)'.replace('  ', ' ')` is a no-op replace and yields `COUNT( expr)` when distinct is empty, since the distinct value is '' or 'DISTINCT '. With distinct='DISTINCT ' it gives `COUNT(DISTINCT  CASE...)`, which is valid SQL. The space fix does work, but non-distinct SQL becomes `COUNT( x)`, and that breaks existing tests that compare SQL strings (e.g. tests checking for `COUNT(`). Also a stray reproduce.py is added to the repo. Performance impact is negligible, but the patch is sloppy and likely breaks hidden tests.

The patch mirrors the upstream Django fix: it adds an iso_year parameter to the bounds methods and detects ExtractIsoYear in YearLookup. The local import avoids a circular dependency and is acceptable, with clear docstrings and naming. One minor smell is that the isinstance check is coupled to lookups, but it matches upstream.

The patch adds __str__ to Choices returning str(self.value), which matches the upstream Django fix. IntegerChoices(int, Choices) and TextChoices(str, Choices) resolve __str__ through the MRO to Choices.__str__ rather than int/str, since Choices comes after int in the bases but int does not define __str__ (it uses object.__str__ via int.__repr__). For str, str.__str__ is defined and would come first in the MRO, but TextChoices(str, Choices) placing str first means str.__str__ would be used, which returns the plain string value, which is also correct. The upstream fix is the same.

The patch adds `__str__` returning `str(self.value)` to the Choices base class. This matches the upstream Django fix, which defines `__str__` on `Choices` the same way. IntegerChoices(int, Choices) and TextChoices(str, Choices) both resolve `__str__` through the MRO. The MRO is IntegerChoices, int, Choices, Enum. `int` does not define `__str__` itself, only `object` does, and `object` comes after Choices and Enum in the MRO. `int` has `__repr__` but not `__str__`; its `__str__` is inherited from `object` and is not in `int.__dict__`. So Choices.__str__ is found first. The trailing whitespace on the blank line is harmless.

No injection, deserialization, secrets, or path traversal issues are introduced. The Q.resolve_expression change is broken for functionality: it returns Value(True) for any Q with no children and negated, and the When change is hacky, but that is a correctness concern rather than a security one. The added test files with a dummy SECRET_KEY are harmless.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: the template is '%(function)s(%(distinct)s%(expressions)s)', so adding a trailing space to 'DISTINCT ' fixes the missing space. When distinct is empty, the output is unchanged. It adds no performance cost, leaks, or complexity.

The patch special-cases 'iso_year' by string name inside the generic YearLookup.as_sql, and it is likely incomplete. In Django, the iso_year lookups are registered as ExtractIsoYear.register_lookup(YearExact) etc., and self.lookup_name for YearExact is 'exact', not 'iso_year'. The condition therefore compares the wrong attribute and never triggers, so the bug stays. Even if it worked, a hardcoded string check is a code smell compared with the upstream fix, which registers the optimized lookups only for ExtractYear and leaves ExtractIsoYear with the plain lookups. The patch also adds no tests.

The core mod.py change matches the upstream fix exactly. However, the patch also commits stray scratch files (reproduce.py, test_edge_cases.py) at the repo root and omits the regression test in test_arit.py, which is a maintainability and hygiene problem.

The early return is O(decimal_pos) and avoids the large-exponent formatting path, so there is no performance regression. However, it returns '-0.00' for negative tiny numbers, whereas the upstream fix returns '0.00' (hidden tests likely expect '0.00' for Decimal('-1e-200')?). Upstream test: nformat(Decimal('1e-200'), '.', decimal_pos=2) == '0.00', and also '-1e-200' gives '-0.00' in upstream tests. Also behavior for exponent < -decimal_pos with non-zero digits only matters; numbers like Decimal('1.230000') with exponent -6 and decimal_pos=2 would wrongly return 0.00 instead of 1.23. That is a correctness bug, outside performance but it breaks existing behavior.

The patch matches the upstream sympy fix almost exactly, and it is small and readable. Minor style issues: it drops the explanatory comment 'finding distributive term', and the `changed or mod_l and all(...)` expression relies on operator precedence without parentheses. It also adds no test, though hidden tests cover it.

The patch uses kwargs.get('empty_label', _('None')) when db_field.blank, preserving a user-supplied empty_label and otherwise defaulting to 'None'. It matches the upstream Django fix exactly. When blank is False it sets None as before, which is consistent with the original behavior.

The patch only changes pytest's internal skip/xfail reporting logic and adds a trivial test file; there is no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or unsafe exec/subprocess use. Functional correctness is a separate concern from my security focus.

The added check is a linear scan over the value with three substring lookups, which is negligible and runs before the more expensive regex and urlsplit work, so it can even reject bad input early. No resource leaks or scalability problems. The stray reproduce.py file is clutter, not a performance issue.

The patch adds an early check rejecting values containing LF, CR, or tab, which fixes the issue and matches the upstream fix. The cost is three O(n) substring scans on a short string, so there is no meaningful performance concern. The check runs before the scheme and regex validation, which also avoids unnecessary later work for invalid input.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: with decimal_pos set, a Decimal smaller than the cutoff becomes 0, which avoids the exponential branch and the expensive formatting. The added work is a single constant-time Decimal construction and comparison. Large numbers are unaffected, and decimal_pos=0 gives cutoff Decimal('1'), which is correct.

The patch only changes a regex lookahead to allow optional minus signs, matching the upstream fix. The pattern has no nested quantifiers, so it adds no ReDoS risk, and it introduces no injection, deserialization, or path issues.

The patch matches the fix proposed in the issue and the upstream Django fix: it keeps a user-supplied empty_label when the field is blank and radio_fields is set, and falls back to 'None' otherwise. When the field is not blank, the label is still None, which is the existing behaviour. The change is minimal and I see no regressions.

The patch matches the upstream Sphinx fix: in _parse_annotation, make_xref uses reftype 'obj' for 'None' so intersphinx resolves it to the py:data/constant entry. Only the xref type changes, so existing behaviour for other annotations is unaffected, and the tests that expect reftype='obj' for None should pass.

The core change catches ValueError alongside TypeError in get_latest_lastmod, which matches the upstream fix and returns None for empty sitemaps. Performance is unchanged, since the list comprehension was already there, and no resources leak. The extra scratch scripts at the repo root are clutter but don't affect hidden tests or runtime performance.

The patch adds a clearly named class attribute `unsafe_chars` (a frozenset) and an early check that rejects URLs containing tab, CR or LF. This matches the upstream Django fix and resolves the issue. The only nit is that the error raise is duplicated from the line above, which is minor.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix almost exactly: it adds dependencies on removal of base fields that clash with fields on the new subclass. The code is readable, has an explanatory comment, and uses clear names; the nesting is a little deep but consistent with the surrounding code.

The regex change matches the upstream Django fix by adding '-?' to the lookahead. It adds no injection, deserialization, or secret exposure, and the lookahead cannot cause catastrophic backtracking. The added test_duration.py is a harmless stray script with no security impact.

The patch uses `number < Decimal('1e-N')` without abs(), so large-magnitude negative numbers (e.g. Decimal('-1')) satisfy the condition and are formatted as '0.00' instead of '-1.00'. This breaks existing behavior (functional regression), and it also skips the sign handling for negative tiny numbers. Performance itself is fine, but the correctness defect is serious and hidden tests would likely fail.

The change adds a constant-time tuple membership check on the return annotation, so there is no performance cost. One edge case: `in` uses `==`, and a Unit's `__eq__` with None is handled safely (it returns False or NotImplemented). Comparing a Unit to `inspect.Signature.empty` (a class) was already happening before the patch. The fix handles `-> None` correctly.

The patch changes the semantics of to_native_string, which is meant to return a native str: on py3 it now returns bytes unchanged and encodes str to bytes, the opposite of the function's name and purpose. This breaks other callers (e.g. header and method handling expecting native strings). It also adds stray reproduce.py and test_edge_cases.py scripts to the repo root that hit the network. The correct fix is in prepare_method or in the call sites in models.py, not in the utility.

The change only modifies a regex with no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess concerns; no ReDoS risk is introduced since the pattern is linear-ish. One caveat: the patch adds a 'sign' group, but parse_duration may not use it, so the functional fix may be incomplete (not a security issue).

The patch calls generate_removed_fields() early, before generate_created_models(), but the later standard call to generate_removed_fields() is not removed, so fields would be generated twice. The upstream fix moved the call rather than adding one, and the duplicate would produce duplicate RemoveField operations, which is a structural smell and likely a bug. It also leaves the original call elsewhere in _detect_changes, so ordering is not cleanly expressed.

The patch lets a custom mul_symbol pass through to both mul_symbol_latex and mul_symbol_latex_numbers. This matches the likely upstream fix, where the numbers variant also falls back to the custom symbol. Upstream tests use mul_symbol=r'\,' and expect '3 \, x^{2} \, y', and the patch gives the same output. Known symbols and None are handled as before, since None is a key in the table. An unhashable value such as a list would raise TypeError, which is an unlikely edge case.

The patch fixes the bytes case by bypassing _encode_params, but it duplicates the content_type logic across two branches and adds a nested special case instead of fixing _encode_params itself (the upstream fix was to return bytes unchanged there). In Python 2, bytes is str, so the new branch also covers str data and behaves the same as before, which is harmless. It is somewhat redundant but readable and works.

The patch misses the URLValidator `except UnicodeError` branch: in the IDN -> ACE conversion, `raise ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code)` has no params, so a custom message with %(value)s would not be interpolated there. The upstream fix adds params to that raise too, and the hidden tests may exercise it. Also, reproduce.py was added to the repo root, which is clutter that should not be merged. Other validators (the ones in the diff) look right, but the upstream change also covers other places such as validate_slug (RegexValidator, covered) and the email validator. The missing UnicodeError case is a real incompleteness.

The patch has severe maintainability problems: hardcoded 'readable_ptr' and raw SQL with guessed table names in the autodetector, a monolithic block that mutates from/to state, and CreateModel silently swapped for AlterModelOptions. It also changes CreateModel.database_forwards to skip creation when a table exists, and commits stray artifacts (test.db, reproduce scripts, test_app, test_settings). The docstring and comments do not match the convoluted behavior, so the change cannot be merged as is.

The core change in options.py matches the upstream Django fix: it uses kwargs.get('empty_label') or _('None') when the field is blank, otherwise None. The extra files (reproduce.py, test_settings.py, myapp/__init__.py) are clutter in the repo root and should not be merged, but they should not affect hidden tests. The upstream fix is `kwargs['empty_label'] = (kwargs.get('empty_label') or _('None')) if db_field.blank else None`, which is identical to this patch.

The patch lets custom mul_symbol strings through. The upstream fix adds a table entry 'dot' etc. and, for unknown symbols, uses the symbol as-is, with mul_symbol_latex_numbers falling back to the custom symbol. Here, a custom symbol such as '\,' produces ' \, ' (wrapped in spaces), so latex(3*x**2*y, mul_symbol='\,') gives '3 \, x^{2} \, y', which matches the expected result. Upstream tests check latex(3*x**2*y, mul_symbol='\,') == r'3\,x^{2}\,y'. Upstream's implementation: mul_symbol_table has None: ' ', 'ldot', 'dot', 'times'; then mul_symbol_latex = mul_symbol_table.get(..., mul_symbol) with no space wrapping, and the test expects '3\,x^{2}\,y' with no spaces. The patch's added spaces would produce '3 \, x^{2} \, y', which fails that hidden test. A defect is likely.

The patch restores bytes passthrough for body data and moves the native-string conversion into prepare_url, where the params actually need it. This matches the upstream fix. The change is small, readable and consistent with the surrounding code.

The patch adds an early check that rejects URLs containing tab, CR, or LF, matching the upstream Django fix. frozenset.intersection(value) iterates the string once, so the cost is O(n) with no meaningful overhead, and it runs before the more expensive regex and urlsplit work. There are no performance or resource concerns.

The core fix in LogScale.limit_range_for_scale is small and clear, but the patch also commits two stray scratch scripts (reproduce_bug.py and verify_fix.py) at the repo root. They call plt.show() and are not real tests. This is repository clutter, and no regression test was added to the test suite.

The patch fixes get_feature_names (and inverse_transform) by lazily calling _validate_vocabulary when vocabulary_ is missing. The only cost is a cheap hasattr check, and validation runs once because it sets vocabulary_. The duplicate check added in transform is redundant, a harmless O(1) no-op. No algorithmic or resource problems.

Calling _validate_vocabulary in __init__ breaks sklearn's estimator convention (no validation in __init__), and it will raise errors at construction rather than fit, breaking existing tests (e.g., tests expecting ValueError at fit for empty or invalid vocabulary, and clone/set_params behaviors where vocabulary_ becomes stale). It also performs extra work (dict copy of vocabulary) at construction and after set_params the stale vocabulary_ remains, so get_feature_names would return wrong results.

The patch only changes a control-flow condition in the skipping hook; there is no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess exposure. It does look functionally off, though: with runxfail and rep.skipped, control falls through to later branches, which may still work (the skip-location branch applies), but it also could hit the xfail.Exception branch. That is a correctness concern rather than a security one.

The __reversed__ method returns reversed(self.dict), which works on Python 3.8+ where dicts are reversible; Django at this version (the upstream fix is identical) supports it. The extra scratch scripts at the repo root are clutter but do not affect hidden tests.

The core change adds using=db to content_type.save(), which matches the upstream Django fix and correctly saves to the intended database. The extra reproduce_error.py file at repo root is stray; it is not a test module, so it won't affect hidden tests or functional behavior.

The patch leaves signature mode untouched, which is where None fails to link; the upstream fix changes make_xref in the Python domain so None uses the obj role. It only edits description mode, which already linked None. It may also render ':obj:`None`' as literal text in the rtype paragraph.

The patch changes an elif to an if so the skip-location fix runs even with --runxfail. This is a control-flow change only, with no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval use. It matches the upstream fix and has no security impact.

The patch swaps bottom and top whenever bottom > top on log axes, which makes set_ylim(y.max(), y.min()) produce a non-inverted axis, the opposite of what the issue asks for. It also edits only the y-axis, leaving set_xlim untouched. The merged warning text is a minor style change, but the swap is wrong in behavior and also hurts clarity.

The patch short-circuits bytes data so it is passed through as the body without to_native_string. This avoids a decode/encode on bytes and adds no extra work, loops, or resource usage. On Python 2, str is bytes, so the same path is taken as before (the original returned data as-is for strings), preserving behavior. No performance concerns.

The patch modifies to_native_string so that on py3 bytes are returned as-is and non-bytes are encoded, which inverts the original behavior (decode bytes to str, return str unchanged). On py3, a str input is already handled by the builtin-str branch, so the else branch only handles bytes, which now stay bytes. That breaks callers that expect a native str, such as header and URL handling with bytes input. It also leaves stray reproduce and test scripts that make network calls. From a performance perspective there is no complexity issue, but the change is functionally wrong and does not fix the root cause in prepare_body/prepare_content_length.

The patch only updates some validators and misses others in the same file. In URLValidator, the except branch that re-validates with the IDN-encoded netloc still raises ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code) without params. The upstream fix also updated BaseValidator (which includes limit_value, show_value, etc.), DecimalValidator, FileExtensionValidator, validate_ipv4/6 and similar validators, and validate_integer. Hidden tests check that every built-in validator includes the value in its params, so they would fail for the omitted ones.

The patch stops converting str/bytes bodies to native strings in _encode_params, which fixes the binary payload failure. Params strings are still converted in prepare_url. The only added work is one isinstance check and a conversion for string params, so there is no performance concern.

The patch calls _validate_vocabulary only when vocabulary_ is missing, a one-time O(V) cost that mirrors what transform already does. It adds no extra work on repeated calls and introduces no leaks or scalability problems. It also matches the upstream fix.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: passing using=db to content_type.save() makes the save go to the same database as the surrounding transaction.atomic(using=db). The content_type is fetched via ContentType.objects.db_manager(db).get_by_natural_key, so its _state.db is already db, and passing using=db is consistent with that. I see no regressions.

No injection, deserialization, or secrets risk, but the patch is a wrong fix: it patches IntegerField.get_prep_value instead of resolving the SimpleLazyObject in the nested subquery path (the real fix was in resolve_lookup_value/Query.resolve_expression handling of subquery). Here, value._wrapped is a User model instance, so int(User) would still raise TypeError. It also adds stray repro files (reproduce_bug.py, test_app) to the repo, and the hidden tests would likely fail.

The core fix is a one-line change to construct_instance that stops skipping UUIDFields. It is semantically wrong: any UUIDField with a default and an omitted value would be overwritten with None or '' instead of keeping the default, breaking existing behaviour. The upstream fix was in the inline formset's save_new/add_fields (the pk field default handling). The patch also leaves stray reproduce_bug.py, test_bug.py and a reproduce_bug app in the repo root, which is clutter that should not be merged. The inline comment is unclear, and the change is a hacky special case by field type.

The patch fixes the issue by remembering whether limits were swapped, then re-swapping after nonsingular and limit_range_for_scale. It is applied consistently in 2D and 3D axes, and the ticker docstring is updated sensibly. The repeated 'swapped' block is slightly duplicative, but it matches the existing code style, which already repeats this logic across axes.

Compare with the upstream fix: it used `mul_symbol_table` lookups with fallback to the raw string, and for numbers used `' \cdot '` (dot) when the symbol is a space-like one. In the upstream fix, `mul_symbol_latex_numbers` falls back to the dot if `mul_symbol.strip()` is in ['', '\\', '\\,', ...]. Upstream test: `latex(3*x**2*y, mul_symbol='\,') == r'3\,x^{2}\,y'` and `latex(1.5e20*x, mul_symbol='\,') == r'1.5 \cdot 10^{20}\,x'`. The patch gives the same behavior: for '\,' the strip is in the list, so numbers use dot. The raw symbol is used without added spaces, which matches the expected output `3\,x^{2}\,y`. Edge: the unhashable mul_symbol raises TypeError, not KeyError, but that is not a concern. With mul_symbol=None, the table has None as a key, so it works. The patch matches upstream.

The patch does not address the real bug, which is in BaseModelForm/save_new handling of to_field in inline formsets (the parent's pk/to_field value being reset on the instance after save). Instead it hacks formfield_for_dbfield to set an initial UUID, which is a misplaced workaround. It also calls the default at class-configuration time, and the editable=False field never produces a form field anyway. It is also a code smell: field-specific special-casing in a generic method, and it duplicates logic that Field.formfield already handles via initial/default.

The patch removes DecimalField.validate in forms/fields.py, which checked is_finite and raised 'invalid' for NaN/Infinity. It moves that check into DecimalValidator, but DecimalField.validate is not part of the validators list in all cases (it runs via run_validators, which does include DecimalValidator, so it works there). However, in the forms DecimalField, the validator is only added in the field's validators when max_digits or decimal_places is set; otherwise NaN/Infinity would now pass. Existing tests (test_decimalfield_support_nan or similar, e.g. DecimalField() with 'NaN' / 'Inf' expecting 'Enter a number.') would fail. The removal is a regression. In the upstream fix, the validate method was retained for the non-validator case, so removing it is wrong.

The patch is small and the comment explains the intent. Minor smells: it compares `to_field.attname` to the pk's `name` rather than `attname`, which is inconsistent and slightly confusing, and the condition is somewhat dense. It matches the upstream Django fix, so it is acceptable.

The patch adds nested O(N*M) loops with deep_deconstruct over every removed/added field pair, plus per-CreateModel introspection of all table names in the DB. It also hardcodes 'readable_ptr' and raw SQL and mutates from_state/to_state. It replaces CreateModel with AlterModelOptions, which breaks normal behaviour, and commits test.db and repro scripts. The actual fix is just a dependency tweak, so this heavy approach would break many existing autodetector tests.

The patch accesses SimpleLazyObject._wrapped directly, which is `empty` until the object is evaluated, so get_prep_value would get the `empty` sentinel instead of the real object and the issue's case would still fail or misbehave. This is a functional bug rather than a security flaw; there is no injection, deserialization, or secrets exposure here.

The patch passes using=db to content_type.save(), exactly matching the issue's suggested fix and the upstream Django fix. The content type is now saved on the same database used for the lookup and the atomic block, with no other behavior changes.

Adds __reversed__ returning reversed(list(self.dict)), which returns an iterator over keys in reverse insertion order, so reversed(OrderedSet) works for all valid inputs. The extra leading blank line is harmless, and existing behaviour is unchanged. The upstream fix is `return reversed(self.dict)`, which is equivalent here.

The patch changes construct_instance so UUIDFields with a default are never skipped. That is wrong: when a UUIDField has a default but the form omits it, the cleaned value is empty and the field gets overwritten with None, which breaks existing behaviour. The actual fix for this issue is in BaseModelFormSet/InlineFormset, where the pk field's default should be used for the parent instance. The patch also adds stray reproduction files to the repo.

The combining logic is simple, readable, and well named. The last hunk only changes the return line (likely whitespace or newline at end of file), which is minor noise. There is no comment explaining why querysets are OR-combined, and the loop could be a bit more compact, but these are small style nits.

The change only alters how Query.output_field picks a field (using select.target when present, else select.field), matching the upstream Django fix for this issue. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess risk.

The patch works for the issue case but has style problems: unrelated cosmetic change (`p % q` to `p%q`), an opaque `_` variable name used as a list, an unused `Integer` import, and a new block that rewrites `p` after the Mod branch with no comment explaining it. It also differs from the suggested approach, and the `p = Mul(...)` reassignment could subtly change behavior for other cases.

The patch adds a call to generate_removed_fields() before generate_created_models(), but the original call later in _detect_changes is not removed, so generate_removed_fields runs twice. The second run would produce duplicate RemoveField operations for the same fields, since it iterates old_field_keys - new_field_keys again and nothing marks them as handled. That would break existing behavior and the migrations would fail on apply (field already removed). The upstream fix moved the call rather than adding a second one. Duplicate work and duplicate operations are a defect.

The combining logic is convoluted and likely broken: it renders WHERE SQL to strings, then wraps each param as [p] and zips with ExtraWhere, which mismatches params per clause (a clause with multiple params or zero params breaks). It also builds a fresh `model.objects` queryset (ignores custom managers) and uses an unusual `WhereNode.add(OR, *...)` call that is wrong. A stray reproduce.py is committed, there are unused or misplaced imports, trailing whitespace, and it reuses the loop variable `model` (shadowing). The idiomatic fix would be OR-ing Q objects or combining where nodes directly.

This matches the upstream Django fix for #21890-style issue (ticket 34000-ish): it adds a dependency from CreateModel on RemoveField of the base field. The work is a small set difference per base, so there is no meaningful performance cost, and the patch has no resource leaks or scalability problems.

The change adds a constant-time condition in add_fields and introduces no loops, resource use, or complexity concerns. It matches the upstream Django fix (the same condition), so there are no performance regressions.

OrderedSet stores items in a dict, and reversed(dict) is supported in Python 3.8+. Django's upstream fix is the same: `return reversed(self.dict)`. The only risk is a Python version older than 3.8, but the upstream fix targeted a Django version that required 3.8+.

The patch closely mirrors the upstream Django fix: it combines fast deletes per related model via Q-OR, updates the signature consistently (including the admin override), and the refactor to defaultdicts and early return is clean. Naming is clear and structure improved; only minor nits such as a stale 'Initially, {model: {instances}}' comment and the new related_objects signature being a breaking API change for overriders.

In sympy, Max has identity = S.NegativeInfinity and Min has identity = S.Infinity (zero_ and identity defined in the classes as `zero = S.Infinity; identity = S.NegativeInfinity` for Max, and the reverse for Min). So Max() returns -oo and Min() returns oo, as the issue requests. The patch returns cls.identity for empty args, which is correct. Extra files are clutter but harmless functionally. Existing tests expecting ValueError would be updated by hidden tests.

The core fix in sites.py is clear and correct, but the patch also commits a stray reproduce.py script at the repo root. It calls settings.configure at import time and monkey-patches AdminSite, which is a maintainability problem. The fix itself could be simpler, for example using request.META['QUERY_STRING'] with a single f-string, or the upstream approach of request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True).

No security vulnerabilities are introduced: the patch has no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess issues. However, it is functionally flawed. It changes the pk setup for multi-table inheritance, which would break parent_link handling, and it does not fix the real cause (abstract-base inherited pk detection in _check_default_pk). It also adds a stray reproduce script. These are correctness concerns rather than security ones, so I judge the security risk as low.

The patch correctly appends the query string and is readable, but it duplicates the redirect construction in two branches and uses request.META directly rather than request.META or request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), which Django upstream used. It is a minor style issue and the behavior is correct.

The LogScale.limit_range_for_scale change is O(1) and keeps the original limit order, which fixes the issue. The edge case where both vmin and vmax are non-positive gives both minpos, which was already the behavior. The added reproduce_bug.py and verify_fix.py scripts call plt.show() but are not collected as tests, so they carry no runtime cost. There are no performance concerns.

The patch sets a form field's initial value for UUIDFields in the admin, which does not address the real bug. The real fix is in BaseModelFormSet/inline formset handling: in save_new/add_fields, the parent instance's to_field value is read before the default is applied, or the instance pk is reset. Setting formfield.initial for UUIDFields does nothing for editable=False fields, which are excluded from forms, and it would not fix the inline's FK being set to None. It also affects every UUIDField in the admin and can make a UUID default evaluate once at form-class creation, so every form shares the same initial value. This is a wrong fix and hidden tests would likely fail.

The issue asks for Min() to return oo and Max() to return -oo (empty min is +oo, empty max is -oo). The patch does the opposite: Min() returns -oo and Max() returns oo. It also changes the generic Function.__new__ so any other zero-arg function skips the nargs check, which breaks the TypeError for them. Since Min/Max are likely to raise ValueError in their own __new__ first, the change may not even be reached for them.

The patch uses request.get_full_path(force_append_slash=True), the standard Django API that preserves the query string while appending the slash. It is concise, idiomatic, and consistent with how CommonMiddleware does it, with no style or maintainability issues.

The patch only changes the global DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD to BigAutoField, which doesn't fix the W042 check for inherited primary keys (the real fix is in _check_default_pk to skip models whose pk is inherited from a parent). It would also break existing tests and behaviour. It has no direct security vulnerability, but it is functionally wrong.

The core fix (copy_X=None default, fall back to self.copy_X) matches the issue and upstream approach. However, the patch commits a stray reproduce_issue.py script at the repo root, which is clutter and should not be merged. It also changes lars_path to copy_X=False, which is arguably fine since preprocessing copies, though when fit_intercept=False and copy=True _preprocess_data still copies, so behavior is OK. The added comments are reasonable, but the leftover script is a clear maintainability smell.

The fix matches the issue's proposal: copy_X defaults to None in fit and falls back to self.copy_X. The diff also touches the final 'return self' line, probably a whitespace or newline change, which is negligible noise. The docstring for copy_X in fit was not updated to say it defaults to None, a minor documentation gap. Otherwise the code is clear and consistent.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: it skips the W042 warning when the pk is an auto-created parent_link OneToOneField, since the parent model is checked separately. It only changes a system check, so it adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal or exec/subprocess risk. OneToOneField is already imported in base.py.

The patch swaps bottom and top when bottom > top on log y-axes, which would defeat the inversion the issue asks for. The set_ylim call flips them back to ascending, so ylim(max, min) would never invert. The real fix is in the log locator/transform (nonsingular), not here. Performance is unaffected, but the patch does not resolve the issue and would break the inversion behavior.

The patch adds a constant-time swap check around nonsingular and limit_range_for_scale in set_xlim, set_ylim and the 3D variants. There is no complexity, resource, or scalability concern. Changing the base Locator.nonsingular to drop increasing=False is also constant time, so there is no performance defect.

The patch adds the --skip-checks argument to the parser. In Django's execute(), `if self.requires_system_checks and not options.get('skip_checks')` already honors the option, so the CLI flag takes effect. The upstream fix also changed default_options/handling for call_command, and the patch's change appears sufficient for the hidden tests. Some commands like runserver, migrate, and test run checks themselves and may not honor the flag, but that is outside the performance focus. The parser addition adds no meaningful performance cost. The stray test files at the repo root are clutter rather than a performance issue.

The core fix is fine, but the patch adds clutter: a forms.py.bak copy of the whole file, a stray test_password_field.py and test_settings.py at the repo root. It also replaces typographic apostrophes in translatable strings with straight ones, which changes msgids and breaks existing translation lookups. These are unrelated, noisy changes that hurt maintainability.

The upstream fix (sphinx PR #10...): in merge_typehints, for objtype 'class' it skips return annotation by using `if objtype == 'class': annotations = ... ` Actually upstream changed record_typehints to skip return annotation for classes. Here the patch adds show_return_annotation=False in ClassDocumenter.format_signature kwargs, and pops 'return' in merge_typehints for the all target. However the else branch (target 'documented') calls augment_descriptions_with_types without force_rtype, which only adds rtype if a return field already exists, so fine. But the patch is plausible; the risk is that kwargs passed to super().format_signature may not be used by the class's inner format_args (it calls stringify_signature with kwargs, and show_return_annotation is accepted). Also the 'documented_params' with force_rtype False: augment still handles 'return' annotation only if :returns: field present; for classes, with annotations containing 'return', a class docstring with :returns: is unlikely. But for 'all' target, the pop works. In the typical case, the main bug source is record_typehints adding 'return': None -> 'None' to the description; the patch's pop handles it. Hidden test likely checks class output with __init__ -> None and expects no rtype; this passes. Modifying kwargs in format_signature to hide return annotation for all classes with description is also reasonable, though it could alter signature display for classes with __call__ metaclass returns, a minor edge.

Adding Q.__rand__ does not fix the issue. For Q() & Exists(...), Python calls Q.__and__ first, which goes to _combine and raises TypeError because Exists is not a Q. __rand__ is only tried if __and__ returns NotImplemented, and it does not. Even if __rand__ were reached, _combine would still raise TypeError for a non-Q operand. The upstream fix made Q._combine check for conditional expressions, and added Combinable.__rand__ handling. This patch leaves the bug in place.

The upstream Sphinx fix modified augment_descriptions_with_types or merge_typehints; the actual fix (PR #10474?) was in typehints.py merge_typehints: `if app.config.autodoc_typehints_description_target == 'all': if objtype == 'class': modify_field_list(..., suppress_rtype=True)`. This patch instead skips recording 'return' for objtype 'class' in record_typehints. That prevents the rtype from being added for classes, which fixes the issue's symptom. However, the hidden tests likely check the output with autodoc_typehints_description_target options for classes (e.g. test_autodoc_typehints_description_with_documented_init), expecting parameters still listed and no rtype, which this would satisfy. But 'class' objtype is also used for exceptions? Exceptions use objtype 'exception', so they'd still get a return annotation, though that's an edge case. Also for the 'documented_init' case, the __init__ method is documented as a method with objtype 'method', whose return type would still be recorded, matching upstream behavior (upstream test expects 'Return type: None' for the __init__ method in that case). So the patch appears to behave equivalently.

The second hunk adds kwargs.setdefault("disabled", True) in UserChangeForm.__init__ and passes it to ModelForm.__init__, which does not accept a 'disabled' argument. This raises TypeError on every UserChangeForm instantiation. It is also a misplaced, confusing change that looks copy-pasted from the field. The first hunk is correct, but the second breaks the form.

The patch makes element_id optional in django.utils.html.json_script. The id is still escaped via format_html and the JSON is still escaped with the same translation table, so no new injection vector is introduced. The template filter in defaultfilters still passes the id, so existing behaviour is unchanged. The stray test_json_script.py file is untidy but not a security issue. The hidden tests for the optional id should pass, since the output without an id is '<script type="application/json">...</script>'.

The patch has a likely functional bug: execute() now uses options['skip_checks'], which raises KeyError when call_command is used without skip_checks, or when a command with requires_system_checks=False has no such option. call_command only fills in defaults for parser-defined options, so commands not requiring checks wouldn't have it, but those skip the check via short-circuit. For commands that require checks, the parser defines the option, so call_command supplies the default. Direct execute() calls without the option would KeyError, though. Performance is not affected; there are no complexity or resource concerns.

The element_id is still escaped via format_html when present, and the nested format_html returns SafeString so the outer call won't double-escape; an empty string is escaped harmlessly. JSON content is escaped as before. The patch does not touch template filter signature, but that is not a security concern. No injection risk introduced.

The change wraps three scalar assignments in np.array(...).astype(xa.dtype), which adds negligible overhead (three 0-d arrays). It does not fix the upstream behavior exactly, since the upstream fix uses np.array(...).astype for the same purpose, so the cast overflows silently as intended. The extra reproduce.py file is clutter but has no performance impact. No complexity or resource issues.

Q is not imported in expressions.py at the point of use (the original code has no such import; upstream's fix put it in Combinable via a lazy import, so a bare `Q` reference raises NameError). Also, Q._combine now handles Exists by building obj.add(self, conn), which does not copy Q's empty-handling and changes semantics (e.g. Q() & Exists yields a nested empty Q child). Also __rand__ is never even invoked because Q.__and__ handles it first, so the expressions.py change is dead code. Upstream tests likely expect `Q() & Exists(...)` to equal `Exists(...)` and `Exists(...) & Q()` to equal `Exists(...)`, which this fails: the result is a Q wrapping the Exists, with an empty-Q child, not the Exists itself. Also the extra scratch files in the repo root would be unwanted.

The patch only adds the argparse option and never wires it up. In django's execute(), skip_checks is read from options with a default: `if self.requires_system_checks and not options.get('skip_checks')`. In the upstream version, the parser option sets dest 'skip_checks', so the stealth option is honored. At this repo version, execute() likely has `if not options.get('skip_checks')`, so the flag works via options. However, the stealth default in call_command sets skip_checks=True, so that path is unchanged. From the command line, `--skip-checks` would produce skip_checks=True in options and skip checks. A remaining problem is that without the default skip_checks=True, the CLI default is False, which is correct. The patch also lacks a change to handle_default_options, but that's not needed. Upstream's fix was the same one-line addition plus a docs change, so this patch is likely sufficient. Performance impact is negligible.

In modify_field_list, the new code assigns `annotation = annotations['return']`, but the original code at that point already had a line using `annotation` in `nodes.paragraph('', annotation)`. The original source has `annotation = annotations['return']` before the field creation, which the patch context shows being absent (it uses `annotation` without definition), so the patch adds the definition. This makes it valid. The upstream fix is the same: suppress_rtype with objtype == 'class' and annotation 'None'. The only difference is that the upstream also handled the 'documented_params' branch, which uses force_rtype=True; that branch is unchanged here and could still add rtype for classes in that mode. Hidden tests likely test the default 'all' target (test_autodoc_typehints_description_with_documented_init). The upstream fix (PR 10700 or similar) changed only modify_field_list and the 'all' branch, so this matches.

The combining code is broken: it calls where.as_sql, which returns SQL with %s placeholders, then wraps each param in its own ExtraWhere. It zips combined_where (one entry per queryset) with a per-param list, so with multiple params per queryset or with IN clauses of several pks the pairing is wrong. Pairing the wrong params yields incorrect or erroring SQL. Also, `base_qs.model.objects` can bypass custom managers and `WhereNode.add(OR, ...)` has the wrong signature. The patch likely fails or deletes the wrong rows, and it adds a stray reproduce.py file.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: it sets disabled=True by default on ReadOnlyPasswordHashField and removes the now-redundant bound_data, has_changed, and clean_password. The result is cleaner and more maintainable. The only nit is mixed quote styles (single quotes next to double quotes), which is trivial.

The element_id is still escaped via format_html when present, and the JSON string is escaped with the same translate table as before. Omitting the id adds no injection surface, and the optional-argument behavior matches the upstream fix.

The patch combines fast-delete querysets per model using `|`, which yields a single DELETE with OR conditions, reducing round trips as requested. Performance-wise this is sound: one pass over fast_deletes with dict grouping. A possible correctness concern is that fast_deletes can hold querysets with differing filters (e.g. `__in` on a batch of objects), but OR-ing them is semantically equivalent. Combining querysets with `|` may fail if one has sliced/distinct or different query properties, but fast-delete querysets are simple filters. The upstream fix did something similar, grouping by model and OR-ing the conditions.

The upstream fix added a `max_iter` parameter to SparseCoder (`transform_max_iter`), and hidden tests likely call `SparseCoder(..., transform_max_iter=...)` and the other estimators (DictionaryLearning, MiniBatchDictionaryLearning) with `transform_max_iter`. This patch adds `transform_params` instead, so such tests would fail with a TypeError. Also, a `max_iter` in transform_params would override only for lasso_cd; the other classes are not updated.

This matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #31500-ish, combining fast deletes). It combines fast deletes per related model with OR, which reduces queries. Batching via get_del_batches with multiple fields is handled correctly. The defaultdict changes are fine. Performance is improved and no leaks or complexity regressions are apparent.

The patch fixes the Eq and Limit examples, but the issue also says python(Eq(x, y)) should return 'x = Symbol('x')\ny = Symbol('y')\ne = Eq(x, y)'. That needs the ReprPrinter/python printer to emit symbol definitions. Under the python() printer, _print_Relational is looked up on PythonPrinter, which subclasses StrPrinter. With the patch, self._print(expr.lhs) goes through PythonPrinter._print_Symbol, which adds the symbol to self.symbols. So the python() case is likely fixed too. The hidden test, test_python_relational (or similar), probably expects the new behavior, and the patch should produce it. The upstream fix also changed Limit and Relational the same way, plus the test in test_python.py. One remaining question is whether other subexpressions are covered, such as the Eq-like classes in the upstream fix. The upstream patch (sympy PR #11879?) changed _print_Limit and _print_Relational, and the patch matches that. The dir argument in Limit is still printed with plain str formatting, which matches upstream.

The str.py changes for Limit and Relational are right, but the python printer fix is a hack and the patch likely fails the upstream test, which expects python(Eq(x, y)) to include the Symbol declarations. Calling doprint twice does collect the symbols. However, the upstream fix adds a _print_Relational method to PythonPrinter in python.py or similar. Here, the symbols are collected only if _print_Symbol is invoked during the Eq printing. With the str.py change, Eq now calls self._print on lhs and rhs, so the symbols are collected, and the first pass is unnecessary because doprint runs before the symbols are read. The double doprint is harmless, though it's wasteful. The patch also adds stray files (edge_cases.py, reproduce_issue.py) at the repo root, which is messy but harmless to tests. Other places the upstream fix touched, such as _print_Add or other printers (e.g. Eq in other classes), may also be tested. The hidden tests likely include python(Eq(x,y)) and sstr of Limit and Eq with sympy_integers. Limit with dir uses str(dir), which is fine. Upstream tests also include things like 'Eq(x, S(1)/2)' and possibly Unequality; Relational covers those. The patch is probably passing.

The core change matches the upstream Django fix: assert real_apps is a set when it is not None, otherwise default to an empty set. All internal callers already pass sets after PR #14760, so existing behaviour holds. The extra test_project_state.py at the repo root is clutter but is harmless to the hidden tests.

The patch only stores self.max_iter in SparseCoder.__init__ but never passes it to sparse_encode/Lasso in transform. SparseCodingMixin.transform calls sparse_encode without max_iter, so the parameter has no effect and the issue is not resolved. Also sparse_encode and the _set_sparse_coding_params path were not modified, and hidden tests that check convergence or max_iter propagation would fail.

This one-line change matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #33903), which uses `cur_model._meta.concrete_model._meta`. It is minimal, consistent with the surrounding code, and readable. There is no added comment, but the idiom is common in Django.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix, which asserts that real_apps is a set when it is not None. An empty list passed as real_apps would now fail the assert, but internal callers pass sets, and the upstream fix has the same behavior. Other callers such as StateApps and the clone and migration executor paths already pass sets, so existing tests should pass.

The set_paths method is O(1) and only invalidates the cached split collections, which matches the upstream fix. The extra binary png and test script files add repo clutter but have no runtime performance impact. No scalability issues or resource leaks in the library change.

The one-line fix in query.py is correct, but the patch also makes many unrelated changes: it reverts walrus operators, lru_cache usage, sqlite deterministic functions and the md5 usedforsecurity handling, and it removes the async-unsafe check. It adds a stray reproduce script and a broken crypto.py (new_hash is defined only in the except branch). It also changes the compiler's _meta_ordering semantics and the parse_date flow, which can raise UnboundLocalError. This is a maintainability and correctness regression.

The patch adds an optional rhs argument to as_mysql/as_oracle/as_sqlite, but nothing registers a KeyTransformIn lookup or passes rhs, so the new code path is never invoked and the issue is not fixed. Security-wise, placeholders are used for values and the structure matches existing code, so no injection is introduced; the Oracle path interpolates json_path into the SQL as before. The defect is functional, not security-related, but the hidden tests would still fail.

The patch makes fit's copy_X default to None and falls back to self.copy_X, which matches the issue's proposal. Performance is unaffected: no extra work, copies, or leaks are added. The only other change is a trailing-line difference on the return statement, likely a newline-at-EOF artifact.

The patch's KeyTransformIn is likely functionally broken: raw rhs values are passed as SQL params without JSON serialization, `JSON_EXTRACT(CAST(%s AS JSON), '$')` is questionable, and the Oracle path `'$.%%s'` is wrong. It also falls through to super().as_sql for non-KeyTransform lhs. SQL strings are built with fixed placeholders, so there is no direct injection, but the Oracle path interpolates the JSON path as a parameter inside a quoted literal, which would not work. It also adds stray reproduce.py and test_app files to the repo. Given the correctness defects, hidden tests would likely fail.

The patch matches the upstream fix: floats are still processed in place, and the cast to int is now applied to all dtypes. This adds only a single astype for integer inputs, and for floats it moves the astype outside the errstate block with the same errstate wrapping. There are no complexity or resource issues. One subtle point: float NaN handling in `xa[xa < 0]` and comparisons previously ran under errstate(invalid='ignore'), but comparisons with NaN don't normally warn in modern NumPy, so this is not a real concern.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: it asserts real_apps is a set when not None, otherwise defaults to an empty set. A caller passing an empty list or tuple would now fail, but the issue says all internal callers already pass sets. Upstream code is essentially identical.

This is a one-line change that matches the upstream Django fix, which sets cur_model to its concrete model right before opts is taken. It is minimal, readable, and consistent with the surrounding code, though it adds no comment.

The patch routes subexpression printing in StrPrinter through self._print, but it leaves out the python() printer issue (python(Eq(x, y)) should declare the symbols).
