The patch adds __add__ and __radd__ to the lazy __proxy__ class, delegating to the cast result. It does O(1) extra work per call, with no leaks or scalability concerns. This matches the upstream Django fix, so it should resolve the issue without performance regressions.

The change adds an `isinstance(estimator, type)` check so classes are deep-copied (with safe=False) or raise a TypeError (safe=True), matching the upstream fix. It introduces no injection, deserialization, secret, path traversal, or exec/subprocess risk. The extra repro and test scripts are harmless.

The regex is a questionable rewrite. `\d{3}` is outside the `-` in the optional group (`-[A-Za-z]{2}|\d{3}`), so a three-digit region like `es-419` would not match as intended. It also drops the `@` variant (e.g. `ca@valencia`) and hyphenated codes with more than three parts (e.g. `zh-hans-cn` is fine, but `sr-latn` only partly). Existing behaviour is likely broken for `@` locales and for numeric regions. The regex is dense and undocumented, and it is long and hard to read.

The patch commits stray scratch files (reproduce.py, test_edge_cases.py) to the repo root, which is a clear maintainability problem. as_set returns the set S, which is semantically wrong for a variable-dependent condition when the first arg is not a lone symbol, and the new as_relational override adds a questionable ValueError. The upstream fix returns self.args[1] only when the first arg is a Symbol-like and raises otherwise, and the docstrings contain trailing whitespace and a non-ASCII character.

The patch reverts __hash__ to hash(self.creation_counter), which stays constant when the field is assigned to a model. Equality still compares creation_counter and model, so objects with the same hash are still distinguished. This matches the upstream Django fix for the issue.

The core change in linkcheck.py correctly catches TooManyRedirects and falls back to GET, with no performance concerns (the retry happens only on failure). The patch also adds an unrelated reproduce script and pins dependencies in setup.py, which is messy, but these don't create performance issues.

The change is a minimal one-line fix that converts DNS_NAME to punycode via the idna codec before make_msgid, matching the issue's proposed fix. The one maintainability concern is that the encoding happens on every message() call, though IDNA encoding of a short hostname is cheap. The upstream Django fix did the same thing in message.py, and a cached punycode version in utils would be slightly cleaner but isn't required.

The change adds an isinstance(estimator, type) check so estimator classes are deep-copied (a no-op for classes) when safe=False, or raise TypeError when safe=True. It introduces no injection, deserialization, path traversal, eval/exec, or secrets issues.

The patch factors the repeated IDNA-encoding idiom into a single, well-named `punycode` helper in django/utils/encoding.py and applies it consistently across mail, validators and html, which improves readability and reduces duplication. The docstring says 'if it's non-ASCII' but the function always encodes; this is harmless because idna encoding of ASCII is a no-op, so it is a minor nit. It matches the upstream Django fix.

The change only adds an isinstance(estimator, type) check so estimator classes are treated as plain objects and deep-copied (classes deepcopy atomically) when safe=False. It introduces no injection, deserialization, secret, path, or subprocess risk, and it matches the upstream fix.

The patch returns self.args[1] (the set) from Contains.as_set, which is semantically wrong for multi-variable or non-trivial cases such as Contains(x, S) where as_set should be the set of x values satisfying it; for a single symbol x it works, which is the upstream fix. The code is small and readable, but it lacks a docstring and a guard for non-symbol first args.

The patch checks `name in merged_indexes` before `merged_indexes[name] = index` is assigned, so the condition is almost always false and the old behavior remains. The actual fix is in xr.where/apply_ufunc, which passes keep_attrs to coordinates, and this patch doesn't touch that. Even if the branch ran, it would add `merged_vars[name].attrs` into the list, which could change merge results.

The change removes a string replace in getmodpath, which only affects the display of test headlines; no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval risk is introduced. The extra test files are harmless.

The patch does not implement sliced prefetch support as the issue requests; it only raises ValueError in one descriptor (ForwardManyToOne), leaving reverse/many-to-many managers untouched. The if/else after a raise is redundant style, and the message is inconsistent with the goal. Hidden tests expecting sliced prefetch to work would fail.

The patch only extends the existing except clause to also catch TooManyRedirects, so the GET fallback runs in one more case. It adds no loops, no new allocations, and no resource leaks. The extra GET request only happens on failure, so the performance impact is negligible. The change matches the upstream fix.

The one-line change returns the set argument, which matches the upstream sympy fix (Contains(x, S).as_set() returns S). It is simple and readable, though it adds no docstring or test. It is acceptable on maintainability and style.

The change adds TooManyRedirects to the HEAD-to-GET fallback; it costs one extra GET only when HEAD hits a redirect loop. The second edit, `(Exception, TooManyRedirects)`, is redundant but harmless. There is no complexity, leak or scalability concern, and the fallback matches the upstream fix. `requests.exceptions` is reachable because sphinx.util.requests exposes the requests module, so the attribute lookup should work.

The patch resembles the upstream fix but with an error-prone edge: when x is a scalar (e.g. xr.where(cond, 1, 0, keep_attrs=True)) and result is a DataArray, it does result.attrs = {} fine. Passing keep_attrs=True into apply_ufunc keeps first-arg attrs, and these are then overwritten. For cond-only DataArray with scalar x, coords attrs set to {} via getattr(None,'attrs',{}), which matches upstream behaviour. Upstream fix is nearly identical, so hidden tests likely pass.

The patch removes a string replace in getmodpath, which only affects how test names are displayed in headlines. It introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or exec/subprocess risk.

The patch only adds the argparse option; it does not change execute(), which determines skipping via options.get('skip_checks') or requires_system_checks. In Django at this version, execute() has `if self.requires_system_checks and not options.get('skip_checks'): self.check()`. So with the flag set, options['skip_checks']=True, which would skip checks. But the upstream fix also changed execute to handle the default: when called via call_command, skip_checks defaults True, and the parser default is now False in the command line path. In call_command, defaults are parsed from parser and then `if 'skip_checks' not in options: defaults['skip_checks'] = True` is applied after parse_args defaults, so parsed defaults would include skip_checks=False and break the call_command behaviour (checks would now run in call_command). Also, the upstream fix modified call_command, and the existing tests would fail.

The patch uses a hacky private flag (`_restore_slice`) set on a queryset and checked via hasattr, which is a code smell. It is duplicated across two descriptors, and the flag is never cleared, so it leaks onto the clone's parent. The slice is just re-applied to the whole filtered queryset, which gives a global limit rather than a per-instance limit (the actual fix uses a window function). A stray reproduce script with a bogus app_label is also committed to the repo root. Poor structure, no docs or tests.

The patch forces combine_attrs='override' for coordinates and restores coordinate attrs after the fact, which diverges from upstream (which fixed this in xr.where by passing keep_attrs as a callable). Forcing 'override' changes behavior for other operations: coordinate attrs now come from the first object, whereas previously with keep_attrs=False (combine_attrs='drop') coordinate attrs were dropped. Existing tests likely expect coordinate attrs be dropped/merged under default settings (e.g., test_apply_dataarray... or arithmetic with keep_attrs False), so this could break them. Also, modifying coord_var.attrs on da.coords.items() may operate on temporary variable copies (DataArray coords yield DataArray objects whose .attrs set on a new DataArray wrapping the same variable; likely shares the variable, but not guaranteed). Also the upstream fix changed the `where` lambda to `keep_attrs = lambda attrs, context: getattr(x, 'attrs', {})` with the coords handled, and the hidden test checks coordinate attrs are preserved. The patch's broad behavior change risks regressions.

The core fix in computation.py is a small, readable one-line change with a clarifying comment. However, the patch commits two scratch scripts (reproduce_where_error.py and test_where_edge_cases.py) to the repo root. They are print-based, not real tests, and would clutter the repository. That is a clear maintainability and style defect. The lambda is also slightly awkward, since a named function would be clearer, and the comment is imprecise: attrs has only one element when x is a scalar, so attrs[1] is missing.

The rewrite is not a correct HNF algorithm. It uses row negation and row operations (subtracting multiples of pivot rows) instead of the column operations HNF requires, so it does not preserve the column-space lattice. The pivot-finding loop is also convoluted and buggy. Zeroing entries to the right of pivots discards information, giving wrong results on e.g. [[5,8,12],[0,0,1]], where the expected [[5,8,0],[0,0,1]] needs column ops. The function also returns the full matrix with all rows, which changes behavior for existing tests that expect columns to be dropped. Existing tests would likely break.

The helper `_filter_prefetch_queryset` is well named, small, and removes duplicated filter logic from the two call sites. It follows the upstream Django approach (Window RowNumber partitioned by field, filtered by marks). It lacks a docstring, but it is private and short. It also mutates the passed queryset's query via clear_limits, which is a mild smell, though the queryset is already a clone in the prefetch path.

The lambda falls back to attrs[0] when only one attrs entry exists, which avoids the IndexError. When x and y are scalars, the only xarray argument is cond, so the result gets cond's attrs; the upstream fix does the same, so the behavior matches. The one-liner is readable, though a comment for the fallback would help. If attrs is empty, attrs[0] would fail, but apply_ufunc always includes at least cond, so that case does not arise.

The patch only removes a string replace of '.[' with '[' in getmodpath, which is the upstream fix for this issue. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or subprocess/eval risk.

The patch breaks object creation: `super(Permutation, cls).__new__(cls)` resolves to `Basic.__new__(cls)` with no args, so `_args` is empty and hashing/equality via `_hashable_content` (which returns tuple(self.array_form)) may still work, but `p.__init__()` is called explicitly and then Python calls `__init__` again after `__new__`. For subclasses with args-taking `__init__`, `p.__init__()` with no args fails. Also `_af_new` is a module-level alias of the staticmethod, and its signature is changed with `cls` as second positional arg; other callers such as `Permutation._af_new(perm)` still work, but `Basic.__new__(cls)` leaves `args` empty, which breaks `.args`, `func(*args)`, and `copy`/`srepr` behaviour that existing tests may check. The real fix made `_af_new` a classmethod and used `Basic.__new__(cls, perm)`, so this deviates and loses args. Most other internal calls like `_af_new` in `__pow__`, `__add__`, etc. still return base Permutation, so subclassing remains incomplete.

The patch changes Q.resolve_expression so any Q with no children and negated returns Value(True), which is hacky and likely wrong; ~Q(pk__in=[]) has a child, so this branch doesn't even handle the real case. The real fix (compile an EmptyResultSet-negated WHERE as an always-true condition) is not implemented properly; the '1=1' fallback in When.as_sql triggers only if the compiled SQL is empty. It may work, but it also adds stray files (test_app, test_case.py, test_settings.py) to the repo root and changes Q behavior for empty negated Q's (~Q() previously a no-op in filters). Performance impact is minor, but correctness risk with hidden tests is notable.

The patch replaces module-level `_af_new` and `Perm` uses with `cls._af_new`/`self._af_new`, which matches the upstream fix. The `__new__` end previously set `_array_form` and `_size` on `Basic.__new__(cls, aform)`, and `_af_new` does the same, so behavior is unchanged. The `isinstance(a, cls)` check can differ for a subclass: `Permutation(sub_instance)` now builds a new Permutation, but the upstream fix does the same. `__pow__` now uses `isinstance(n, Permutation)`, which is fine. `module-level _af_new = Perm._af_new` still works as a bound classmethod to Permutation. Other callers such as `Perm.unrank_lex` and `PermutationGroup` are unaffected. `unrank_nonlex` still uses `self` as cls, so `self._af_new` works. `rmul_with_af` is now a classmethod, and callers like `Permutation.rmul_with_af(...)` still work. The upstream fix is essentially the same.

The patch adds an empty-name check raising ValueError before the dot check, which matches the issue and the upstream fix. The trailing 'return f' diff is only a whitespace/newline change and does not alter behavior.

The lambda now reads attrs directly from x via getattr(x, "attrs", {}), which handles scalar x and matches the upstream fix. It is concise and clear, with a small style blemish: the blank line after the keep_attrs default was removed, which is cosmetic. The existing comment still describes the intent accurately.

The patch changes _af_new to a classmethod but leaves other code that creates instances via the module-level alias `_af_new = Perm._af_new`. That alias is now a bound method of Permutation, so existing calls still work and return Permutation. However, the patch does not update __new__ or other methods (e.g. __mul__, inverse) to use cls/self.__class__, so subclasses still get Permutation instances from most operations. The real upstream fix changed __new__ to use cls._af_new and many other places such as `_af_new(...)` to `self._af_new(...)`. Hidden tests likely check that a subclass instance is created via the constructor, and Permutation.__new__ calls `cls._af_new(...)` only if changed. Here __new__ still calls the module-level `_af_new`, or `Basic.__new__(cls, ...)` in other branches, so a subclass built from a list likely returns Permutation. The patch is incomplete and likely fails the hidden tests.

The patch adds a ValueError for empty or whitespace-only names in Blueprint.__init__, placed after the dot check. This matches the upstream fix (`if not name: raise ValueError("'name' may not be empty.")`), and the hidden test likely only checks `Blueprint("", __name__)` raising ValueError. Rejecting whitespace-only names is a minor extra restriction and unlikely to break existing tests. The extra files (reproduce.py, test_edge_cases.py) are clutter but don't affect behavior; the test_edge_cases.py name could be collected by pytest, but it would only run at import/collection time and shouldn't fail.

The patch only flips the default of check_rank to True, which does not fix the bug. The real issue is that _hermite_normal_form drops rows when the matrix has more columns than rows and the pivot search fails for a column (the matrix is 3x2 after transposing, with a zero pivot). With check_rank=True the function would instead raise DMRankError for rank-deficient matrices, or the rows are still dropped. The actual fix changes the algorithm so that it handles the zero columns correctly. The patch also changes the default behaviour and would break existing tests that expect rank-deficient matrices to return a reduced result.

The patch adds get-pip.py, a ~24k-line base85-encoded blob that downloads and executes pip when run, plus a stray edge_cases.py script that makes real network requests. Neither is related to the issue. The opaque binary payload is a supply-chain risk and cannot be audited in review. The actual fix in sessions.py is not visible in the truncated patch, so I cannot confirm it exists.

The mode property itself is a reasonable fix, but the patch commits a stray reproduce.py at the repo root, which depends on youtube_dl, is not a real test, and would be collected by pytest. It also adds no regression test or changelog entry, and returns None when the buffer has no mode, which differs from the original AttributeError behavior. These are maintainability defects.

The patch adds a trivial empty-string check in When.as_sql and compiles Value(True) as a fallback, which is O(1) and only runs in the rare empty-condition case. It matches the upstream Django fix (which used a Value(True) fallback), and it has no performance, scalability, or resource issues.

The change converts the method to a native str before upper(), which fixes the Python 2 unicode issue. It adds no injection, deserialization, secret, path traversal, or exec risk. A bytes method on Python 3 would become "B'GET'", but that is a functional concern rather than a security one, and the upstream fix was similar.

The patch only changes the When() constructor check, which doesn't fix the crash. ~Q(pk__in=[]) is a non-empty Q, so that check never fired for it. The failure is in SQL compilation: the compiler raises EmptyResultSet for the inner condition, which gets swallowed into an empty string. Django's real fix was in When.as_sql, catching EmptyResultSet on the condition and adding a NegatedExpression check in Case.as_sql. The patch also makes an empty negated Q() (~Q()) pass validation, and that would likely generate broken SQL. Performance is not the issue here, but the patch doesn't resolve the bug, so hidden tests would fail.

The regex change `(?i)` at the start works for the fix, but the patch includes unrelated changes: pinning setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml and a stray test_qdp.py scratch script at repo root that writes files and has no assertions. These are maintainability and style defects (scope creep, build constraint pollution, junk file). The core fix also does not handle the lowercase 'no' token in data lines or the _get_tables_from_qdp_file handling of command case, e.g. `command[1].lower()` is not applied, so 'read serr' would likely fail later with 'SERR' comparisons.

The patch converts the method to the native str type via builtin_str before upper(). This introduces no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess risk. On Python 3 with a bytes method, builtin_str(b'GET') yields "b'GET'", which is a functional quirk but not a security flaw. It matches the upstream fix.

The patch adds re.IGNORECASE to the line-type regex and makes the NO check case-insensitive, which is minimal and consistent with the upstream fix. The downstream command parsing already handles case: in _get_tables_from_qdp_file, `command = line.strip().split()` with `command[1].lower() == 'serr'` is already lowercase-tolerant upstream. The style is clean and the change is small and readable, though there are no comments or tests.

The scoped inline flag `(?i:...)` requires Python 3.6+, which astropy supports, so the regex change is fine. It is a minimal, readable change. However, the rest of the code may also assume uppercase: `_get_tables_from_qdp_file` uses `line.split()` and `command[1].lower()` is probably used for 'serr'/'terr' type, and the NO handling is also relevant. In the upstream fix, the regex became `re.compile(_command_re, re.IGNORECASE)` and `command[1].lower()` was already used, so this patch likely suffices. Also, `_line_type` matches with `re.compile(...)` on a full string, so the inline flag works. Style is acceptable, though no tests or docs were added.

The patch registers '--skip-checks' four times on the same parser. argparse raises ArgumentError ('conflicting option string: --skip-checks') on the duplicate add_argument call, so the runserver command crashes whenever its parser is created. Beyond that, the upstream fix also needs the inner_run and skip_checks handling (e.g. in the reloader path and in BaseCommand's requires_system_checks), and this patch's options['skip_checks'] use might not be consistent with that.

Small, focused property that mirrors the existing `name` property pattern and matches the upstream fix. It lacks a docstring, unlike the neighbouring `name` property, but this is a minor style nit. Naming, placement and structure are fine.

The standard rotation matrix has m12 = 2(cd - ba) and m21 = 2(cd + ba), so the patch's m12 change is correct for the issue's example (rotation about x gives [[1,0,0],[0,cos,-sin],[0,sin,cos]]). m21 stays positive, which matches. The upstream fix made this same change. The remaining entries (m01, m02, m20 and so on) were already correct in the original code.

The core fix (setting self.data.cols and calling _set_col_formats) is similar to the upstream fix, but the patch also commits a stray reproduce.py debug script and pins setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml, which are unrelated and harmful for maintainability. The extra hasattr(col.info, 'format') block is redundant noise as well, and a stray whitespace-only change adds more diff clutter.

The patch only strips 'b' from the mode passed to os.fdopen, but the real fix needs EncodedFile.mode to not advertise 'b'. In the upstream fix, EncodedFile gained a `mode` property returning `self.buffer.mode.replace('b', '')`, and fdopen still used binary mode. Here, opening with a text mode and buffering=0 raises ValueError on Python 3 ("can't have unbuffered text I/O"), so this likely breaks capture entirely. It is also a poor structural change: it alters the underlying file type instead of fixing the advertised attribute.

The patch replaces the stored canvas attribute with a property that reads ref_artist.figure.canvas, which matches the upstream fix. The added cost is one attribute lookup per access, which is negligible, and it introduces no leaks or complexity problems.

No injection, deserialization, eval, or path-traversal risks in the compiler change; it only calls field.from_db_value on returned values. The patch does commit a stray db.sqlite3 binary and a reproduce script, which is poor hygiene but not an exploitable vulnerability. Functional issues exist (hasattr on all fields, rows possibly tuples so row[i] assignment may fail), but those are outside the security focus.

The template change is a hacky `.replace('  ', ' ')` on a literal string that is a no-op, and the added space yields `COUNT( expr)` when distinct is empty, which changes SQL output and likely breaks existing tests that compare SQL strings. The correct fix is `'DISTINCT '` in the distinct value. The patch also commits a stray reproduce.py to the repo root.

The patch only sets `legend` to None in the pickled state, but the DraggableOffsetBox/DraggableBase still holds `canvas`, `ref_artist`, and callback ids. The canvas (FigureCanvasQTAgg) is unpicklable, so the original error would persist; the upstream fix modified `DraggableBase` to drop the canvas and `ref_artist` and to handle unpickled state. The performance concern is not an issue here, but the patch is functionally incomplete and would fail the hidden tests.

The patch only substitutes a constant Value(True) when the compiled condition SQL is empty, with no user input interpolation, no eval/exec, no deserialization, and no file access. It introduces no security vulnerabilities and matches the upstream Django fix.

The patch only relaxes the empty-Q check for negated Qs and adds no injection, deserialization, secrets or path-traversal risk. It likely does not fix the bug, because ~Q(pk__in=[]) is not an empty Q (it has a child), so the check was never what failed. The real bug is in the compiler, where the EmptyResultSet is mishandled inside Case/When. This is a functional correctness concern, not a security one.

The patch sets requires_system_checks = '__all__' on runserver, so BaseCommand.run_from_argv/execute runs checks before handle() (unless skip_checks). In the inner_run, checks are then run again when not skipped. That duplicates checks, and in the autoreloader the outer process also runs checks before starting the reloader, which changes behavior (the upstream fix kept requires_system_checks = [] and added skip_checks to the parser). Also, with '__all__' the base execute does checks only if not skip_checks, and skip_checks is in options only when added to the parser; the BaseCommand adds --skip-checks only if requires_system_checks is truthy, so the option now exists. But runserver's handle sets options skip_checks... The upstream fix: requires_system_checks=[], add_arguments adds '--skip-checks', inner_run checks if not skip_checks. Here, checks run twice and tests expecting a single check output (e.g., tests counting check calls) may fail. It also adds a stray test script and sets DEBUG=True in test settings, which could break existing tests.

The patch mutates the input table's column formats (col.info.format) in place, a side effect on the user's table; upstream fix uses a copy of the columns' formats via self.data._set_col_formats() after setting cols. Also the patch sets format on the original table, which may leak and persist, and it bypasses the established mechanism in core. The diff also changes the trailing newline at end of file. Functionally it likely works for callable formats, since col.info.format accepts callables, but the mutation is a notable code smell.

The patch adds two lines mirroring how the base writer sets up columns and formats (self.data.cols and _set_col_formats), matching the upstream fix. It is minimal, consistent with existing code style, and introduces no maintainability issues.

The patch's __getstate__ in DraggableLegend drops 'ref_artist' and 'offsetbox', but DraggableBase stores 'ref_artist' and the legend's draggable holds 'legend'. Unpickling a figure whose legend has a draggable runs __setstate__, which sets self.canvas = None. The DraggableOffsetBox __setstate__ is overridden by the subclass, so it does not run. The Figure pickle path calls self.canvas.callbacks... only when needed. There is a likely bug: DraggableBase has a disconnect method using self.canvas and _c1, and the canvas is None until _ensure_canvas runs. Also, _ensure_canvas uses legend.parent.canvas, but Legend.parent is an Axes (no canvas attribute), so this would raise AttributeError after unpickle. The pick connection ('pick_event' via _cid_pick) is also not restored, so dragging is broken after unpickle. Performance-wise there are no complexity issues, but stray files (reproduce_error.py, test_draggable_legend.py) are added at repo root, and the functional correctness problems are significant. The upstream fix uses a different approach (the canvas as a property).

The patch applies field converters to the rows returned from insert, matching the upstream Django fix. It adds no injection, deserialization, path traversal, secret handling, or eval/subprocess exposure, and the converters it runs are field-defined hooks that already run on query results.

The patch adds --skip-checks and gates the checks in inner_run, but in this Django version BaseCommand.execute only skips its own checks when options.get('skip_checks') is set, and runserver has requires_system_checks = False. Upstream's fix does the same: it adds the argument, wraps the check in inner_run with `if not options['skip_checks']`, and sets skip_checks in options. A possible KeyError: tests call inner_run or call_command('runserver') with options missing skip_checks. call_command goes through parser defaults, so skip_checks gets set to False, and the real command path is also fine. The upstream fix is essentially identical, so the patch should pass.

Prepending a space to Case.template is a hack that fixes COUNT(DISTINCTCASE...) but leaves the root cause in Aggregate's template ('%(function)s(%(distinct)s%(expressions)s)'), which should have a space in the distinct value. It also changes Case SQL output everywhere, with leading whitespace that could break tests comparing SQL strings and is an inelegant style smell.

The patch is functionally broken, though not a security vulnerability. It calls field.from_db_value(value, None, using, None) with wrong arguments (the signature is value, expression, connection) and passes the alias string instead of a connection. Fields without from_db_value, such as AutoField, would raise AttributeError. It also does not touch the Model._save_table path that sets attributes, and execute_sql returns a list of rows only in some cases, so it may break for single-object inserts. No injection, deserialization, secrets, or path traversal issues were introduced.

The patch clips the rectangle to the axes limits in _draw_shape, but the actual bug is that the span rectangle and handles are created at 0 and added to the axes, which triggers autoscale to include 0. The real fix is to create the rectangle with zero extent at the axes limits or to disable autoscale updates (e.g. via ax.add_patch plus a _update_dataLim fix). Clipping in _draw_shape does not address the initial rectangle at 0, and the interactive handles are also still at 0. The patch also adds a stray reproduce_issue.py file. Performance cost is trivial, but it does not resolve the issue, so hidden tests would likely fail.
The patch iterates over all rows from the bottom and stops once k reaches 0, which matches the upstream sympy fix. This addresses the dropped-row case in the issue.

The upstream fix was `if 'get_%s_display' % self.name not in cls.__dict__:`. This patch uses `hasattr(cls, ...)`, which also finds inherited attributes. That breaks the case of an abstract or concrete parent model with a choices field: a child that redefines the field with different choices would inherit the parent's partialmethod bound to the parent's field, so it would use the wrong choices. Fields inherited from abstract bases are copied and contribute_to_class is called on the child, and hasattr would then be True from the parent's display method, leaving the parent's field in use. Django's existing tests (e.g. test_overriding_inherited_FIELD_display in model_fields tests) cover overriding choices in an abstract child, and this would fail them. Related: the multi-table inheritance case is also affected.

The change builds Q objects using keyword dict lookups from admin-configured search_fields and passes user input only as parameter values, so there is no injection, deserialization, secret, or path traversal risk. The added reproduce.py uses only an in-memory sqlite DB with hardcoded data and is harmless, though it is clutter.

The core fix is correct and matches the upstream Django fix (catching ValueError alongside TypeError). However, the patch also commits three stray scratch scripts (minimal_reproduce.py, reproduce_sitemap_error.py, test_fix.py) at the repo root, which is clutter and a maintainability problem; test_fix.py even tests a re-implemented copy of the function rather than the real code. The real fix is a one-line change, so the extra files should be removed before merging.

The patch initializes edge handles at the axes bounds instead of self.extents (which are 0,0 before a selection), so no autoscale expansion to include 0 occurs. This matches the upstream fix, and it adds only two cheap getter calls with no performance concerns.

This matches the upstream Django fix (hasattr check before setting get_FOO_display), so a user-defined override on the class is preserved. Inherited cases are also handled in the upstream fix the same way, so behavior should match the hidden tests.

The core fix (int(round(...))) in both places matches the issue and is correct. However, the patch commits stray scratch files (reproduce_error.py, test_edge_cases.py) to the repo root and changes a file mode, which are maintainability/hygiene flaws; the duplicated expression is minor.

The patch moves the trailing space into the 'DISTINCT ' value, and the Aggregate template is '%(function)s(%(distinct)s%(expressions)s)'. That gives 'COUNT(DISTINCT CASE...' and 'COUNT(DISTINCT col)', and the non-distinct case stays 'COUNT(col)'. This matches the upstream fix. The change is minimal and readable.

The one-line change mirrors the upstream Django fix (catching ValueError alongside TypeError) and is minimal, consistent with the existing code style, and readable. It resolves the empty-items case without adding smells.

No injection, deserialization of untrusted data, or path issues are introduced. However, the patch likely doesn't fix the pickling problem, since the canvas reference lives in DraggableBase (self.canvas, motion callbacks), which this patch leaves untouched; setting legend=None also breaks the draggable after unpickle. This is a correctness concern rather than a security one.

The patch makes _get_FIELD_display call get_<attname>_display, which is the same method that contribute_to_class installs as a partialmethod calling _get_FIELD_display. This causes infinite recursion for every field with choices that has no override. Even with an override, calling super() or the default would recurse infinitely. The correct fix is in contribute_to_class, which should only set the method if it is not already defined on the class.

The patch replaces the stored canvas attribute with a read-only property derived from ref_artist.figure.canvas, which fixes pickling. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess risk.

The patch only rewrites how the OR Q object is built, using Q(**{lookup: bit}) with the same lookups and values. It does not fix the multi-join problem from the issue, but it adds no security risk: no injection, deserialization, secrets, or path traversal. Lookup names come from admin configuration and the user input remains a parameterized value.

No injection, unsafe deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess issues; the added __getstate__/__setstate__ only manipulate object attributes, and the pickle handling doesn't introduce new attack surface beyond standard pickle. Functional correctness concerns exist (e.g. DraggableLegend __setstate__ may leave state inconsistent, stray files added) but these are outside the security focus.

The one-line change uses max(..., default=None), which cleanly handles empty items and matches the upstream Django fix. It is readable, idiomatic, and keeps the existing TypeError handling without adding complexity.

The patch only clips rectangle coordinates to axes limits and adds a harmless repro script; there is no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess usage. Functionally it may not fix the root cause, but that is outside the security focus.

The one-line change wraps the computation in int(round(...)), matching the fix proposed in the issue. It is minimal and readable, and the inline expression is clear enough. Other places in optics_.py (e.g. cluster_optics_xi, min_cluster_size) are outside this issue's scope.

Adding a leading space to the Case template fixes 'COUNT(DISTINCTCASE' but changes the SQL text of every Case expression, which could break hidden tests that compare SQL strings. The upstream fix instead changed Aggregate's template to 'DISTINCT ' with a trailing space. The performance impact is negligible, but the patch deviates from upstream and risks correctness regressions.

The patch only changes json.dumps for a boolean in the autocomplete widget's data-allow-clear attribute. It never touches JSONField's form field (forms.JSONField.prepare_value) or the model field's formfield, which is where the unicode escaping occurs. The issue remains unresolved and hidden tests for JSONField unicode display would fail. There is no performance concern, but the patch is functionally wrong.

The patch only changes the initial position of an invisible Rectangle to infinity so it does not affect autoscale limits. There is no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/exec/subprocess use, so it raises no security concerns.

The patch removes the premature '' to ' replacement in _split, so unescaping happens once in _parse_value on the rejoined value. It also anchors the comment regex with $. This appears to match the upstream astropy fix and should resolve the inconsistency without breaking other behaviour.

The upstream fix changed forms.JSONField.prepare_value to pass ensure_ascii=False and added it to model JSONField's get_prep_value path in the admin. This patch instead changes DjangoJSONEncoder's default globally, which doesn't fix the admin form field: forms.JSONField.prepare_value calls json.dumps(value, cls=self.encoder), and with encoder=None the plain JSONEncoder is used, so ensure_ascii stays True. The hidden tests (e.g. test_prepare_value / test_redisplay_wrong_input with unicode) would likely fail, and the global change also alters serializer output and could break existing tests. The stray reproduce_error.py is also clutter.

The patch wraps the float-derived values in int() in all three places, which fixes the TypeError. Docstrings are corrected to match behavior (default=5, int-only for the private _xi_cluster). It uses truncation rather than rounding as the issue suggested, but the 'rounded to be at least 2' docs remain loosely accurate. The code is consistent, minimal and readable.

The patch only changes the initial position of edge handle lines to use the axis bounds instead of the extents. It adds no injection, deserialization, secrets, path traversal, or eval/subprocess risk, so there is no security concern.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False in both the form field's prepare_value and the admin display. It adds no algorithmic overhead, since the same single serialization still happens. The TypeError fallback is preserved, and json.dumps with cls=None is fine.

The patch swaps the alignment branches in _get_aligned_offsets so 'bottom' gives offsets of d (aligned at the bottom) and 'top' gives height - h + d (aligned at the top). This matches the upstream fix. For VPacker, which passes align left/right through the same function, 'left' keeps the same offsets as before and 'right' is unchanged, so VPacker behavior is preserved.

The patch has a correctness bug: `number < Decimal('1e-N')` is true for all negative numbers, so e.g. Decimal('-5') with decimal_pos=2 would format as '0.00'. It also adds a stray blank line at the top and alters the final line's newline. Nesting is deepened and the zero-handling is awkward; the upstream fix used a cleaner approach.

The fix rounds float min_samples to int in both compute_optics_graph and cluster_optics_xi, matching the upstream fix. The int(round(...)) call is O(1) with no added complexity or resource use. The stray reproduce/test scripts are clutter, not a performance problem.

The patch converts the float min_samples to an int with one extra rounding call, which has negligible performance cost and fixes the NearestNeighbors TypeError. Other code paths, such as cluster_optics_xi and the OPTICS.fit min_samples handling, may have similar issues, but they are not part of this issue or the performance focus.

The fix is small and readable, but it leaves a stray reproduce.py script in the repo root, which is a clear maintainability problem. The new code also adds trailing whitespace on blank lines. It changes behaviour for every small decimal (e.g. Decimal('0.001') with decimal_pos=2 gives '0.00', which is probably fine), but it also returns '-0.00' for negative values. Upstream Django's fix returns '0.00' for the Decimal('-1e-200') case, so hidden tests may expect no minus sign. The early return also bypasses the existing flow.

The patch is small and clear, with a helpful comment, and matches the upstream Django fix. The cutoff construction via '1'.rjust is slightly cryptic but readable, and the blank line after the if is a minor style nit.

The fix works for `-> None`, but the patch commits stray poc.py and poc_optional.py files at the repo root, which is clutter and a clear maintainability flaw. The Union/Optional handling is over-engineered and unneeded: `Optional[None]` collapses to NoneType, and Union with None would return unconverted values, silently skipping unit conversion. The logic is also redundant: the `return_ is not None` check plus the final `return return_` makes the flow convoluted, and the typing branch is untested and speculative.

The patch initializes the Rectangle at (inf, inf) instead of (0, 0), which is likely to stop autoscaling from including 0. But it is not the upstream fix, which used `self.ax.get_xbound()` / `ax.get_ybound()` to set the initial rectangle and the interactive handle lines. Inf coordinates may cause problems elsewhere, such as NaN in the data limits or the handle lines. Rectangle with inf xy: when added to the axes via add_patch, update_datalim uses the patch's get_path/transform, and the data limits could become inf/nan. The Axes.update_datalim ignores non-finite points (it uses `np.isfinite` in `update_from_data_xy`), which is why the rect with inf may work. Upstream tests check `ax.get_xlim()` and the rect's position after creation. The upstream fix was `self._rect = Rectangle((0, 0), w, h, ...)` followed by `ax.add_patch` after `self.new_axes`, plus `_setup_edge_handle`. Hidden tests probably check that the limits are unchanged, which this should satisfy. Performance is not a concern here, and the behavior is likely OK.

The regex change matches the upstream fix exactly, with a lookahead that adds optional minus signs. It adds no meaningful backtracking risk, since the pattern is linear and bounded. The stray test_duration.py script is clutter but has no performance impact.

The change is a minimal guard (`return_ is not None`) that fixes the issue; the long condition line is slightly awkward and the unrelated end-of-file diff on `quantity_input` is likely only whitespace/newline noise. Readability is acceptable, though the upstream fix checked the annotation for None instead.

The patch truncates the float-derived min_samples to an int via int(min_samples * n_samples), which fixes the NearestNeighbors TypeError. It also applies the same fix in cluster_optics_xi. There is no performance regression: the added work is a constant-time int conversion. Truncation instead of rounding is a minor semantic difference, but the upstream fix does the same thing.
The patch matches the upstream Django fix: it only adds optional minus signs to the lookahead. The lookahead is bounded and adds no meaningful backtracking, so there is no performance regression.

The upstream fix changes the message to "expected 'time' as the first columns but found 'time'" -> "TimeSeries object is invalid - expected ['time', 'flux'] as the first columns but found ['time']". Hidden tests likely match that message via pytest.raises(match=...), e.g. "TimeSeries object is invalid - expected 'time' as the first column but found 'time'" being replaced by "expected ['time', 'a'] ..." or similar. The patch's messages ("missing required column") won't match those. Existing tests like test_required_columns match "expected 'time' as the first column but found 'a'" in other cases (e.g. when time is not first), and the patch changes that message to "columns must be in order" or "missing required column", which would break them. The patch also adds stray files and changes pyproject.toml's setuptools pin, which is unrelated.

The patch changes DjangoJSONEncoder to default ensure_ascii=False, which does not introduce injection or deserialization issues in itself. It does matter for security that the serializer output is also used in HTML contexts (json_script uses its own escaping and passes cls=DjangoJSONEncoder, and still escapes <, >, & afterward), so no XSS regression. Also, the patch does not touch the admin JSONField form (forms.JSONField.prepare_value uses json.dumps with ensure_ascii default), so it likely does not fix the issue and hidden tests would fail. That is a correctness gap rather than a security defect. The stray reproduce_error.py is harmless.

The patch only changes json.dumps of a boolean in the autocomplete widget, which does not touch JSONField handling. It does not fix the issue (JSONField.prepare_value / get_prep_value needs ensure_ascii=False), so hidden tests would fail. There are no security concerns, but the patch is functionally wrong.
The patch swaps the offset formulas for top and bottom in _get_aligned_offsets, which is the fix the issue asks for. Left and right behave as before, so VPacker is unaffected.

The patch changes the message for every mismatch to a 'missing required columns' form. If columns are all present but in the wrong order, missing_columns is empty and the message becomes "missing required column ''", which is wrong. The existing tests also expect the old message, e.g. "expected 'time' as the first column but found 'c'" in test_required_columns, so the hidden tests would likely fail. The upstream fix keeps the old message for the case where the first column is wrong and adds a separate branch for missing columns, which this patch does not do.

The patch calls validation in __init__, which violates scikit-learn's convention that constructors only store parameters and do no validation (breaks clone/set_params, and get_params semantics). It also leaves stray scratch scripts (reproduce_error.py, test_edge_cases.py) in the repo and adds trailing whitespace. The correct fix is to call _validate_vocabulary in get_feature_names via _check_vocabulary.

The validator change is small, clear and correctly placed, matching the upstream fix (reject LF/CR/TAB early). However, the patch also commits a stray reproduce.py scratch script at the repo root, which is clutter that should not be merged.

The fix handles `-> None` correctly: `annotation is not None` is False, so `return_` is returned unchanged. The extra checks are O(1) per call and add no meaningful overhead or resource problems. Stray poc files in the repo root are clutter but not a performance issue, and the hidden tests should pass.

The functional fix in get_feature_names and inverse_transform is correct, but the patch adds a redundant duplicate block in transform: the identical `if not hasattr(self, 'vocabulary_'): self._validate_vocabulary()` now appears twice in a row. This is a clear copy-paste code smell that a reviewer would ask to remove. The same guard is also now repeated in three places rather than being factored into a helper.

The patch only changes json.dumps to use ensure_ascii=False for display and form prepare_value, matching the upstream Django fix. It adds no injection, deserialization, path traversal, or exec/subprocess risk. Output is still escaped by the template or format_html layer, and the admin display path already returned a string that gets autoescaped.

The change is a minimal, readable one-line fix that skips the unit conversion when the return annotation is None. The tuple membership check works, and `in` falls back to == comparison, which is fine for unit annotations since Unit.__eq__ with None returns False. No documentation or naming problems, though a changelog entry and test would be nice.

The patch adds a constant-time `return_ is not None` check before calling `.to`, so there is no added algorithmic cost, resource use, or scalability problem. It also fixes the `-> None` constructor case. The trailing newline change on the last line is cosmetic. The upstream fix is similar, though it also checks `return_annotation is None` instead of only the returned value.

The patch mirrors the upstream fix: get_feature_names calls _validate_vocabulary when vocabulary_ is not yet set, then _check_vocabulary. It is small, consistent with how transform handles this, and follows existing naming and structure. The docstring is unchanged but was already minimal.

Passing (h, h - yd) as the descent breaks alignment. With yd=0, 'bottom' gives offsets equal to each child's height (20 and 30), so children are not bottom-aligned. 'baseline' also gets wrong descents, and the label swap is never fixed in _get_aligned_offsets.

The early check rejects URLs containing LF, CR or tab, which matches the upstream Django fix (which used a `unsafe_chars` check). It is readable and well placed with a comment. The minor nit is that the hardcoded tuple and the generator expression could be a class constant, but this is a small style point.

Performance is unaffected: the patch only adds one cheap xfail-marks evaluation under --runxfail and a few boolean checks, with no complexity or leak issues. Separately, the patch likely breaks behavior: it removes the 'elif runxfail: pass' branch, so xfail-marked tests under --runxfail would be converted to xfailed/xpassed, and it changes the skip-location logic. That is a correctness problem outside my performance focus, and I weight it heavily because hidden tests would fail.

The patch adds a 'sign' group to the regex but the diff does not touch parse_duration, which must apply the sign to the parsed values. Without that change, the sign is ignored and negative durations get wrong results. The upstream fix did use a sign group, but it also changed parse_duration to handle it, so this patch is incomplete. It also breaks existing behavior: inputs like '-1 day, -00:00:01' or '-15:30' no longer parse as before, since hours and minutes lose their individual signs. Regex performance itself is fine, with no backtracking concerns.

The patch matches the upstream astropy fix: the error message now lists all the required columns and the columns actually found, using the same helper. Single-column messages keep the old format, so existing tests still pass.

The patch hardcodes URLs for only None and int and a Python v3.8 title, instead of using the cross-reference machinery (pending_xref with py:class) that the real fix uses. It also changes merge_typehints so that signature mode populates annotations. In signature mode, 'annotations' are never recorded for signature-mode behavior, and the real fix is in sphinx/domains/python.py (type_to_xref). The setup.py dependency pins are unrelated. Hidden tests for the real fix would check for pending_xref nodes in the signature, which this patch does not produce. Other types (str, float) would remain unlinked, and the 'description' mode now emits hardcoded external links rather than resolved xrefs, which changes existing behavior.

The patch removes the empty-args ValueError, and the rest of MinMaxBase.__new__ already returns cls.identity for an empty arg set (oo for Min, -oo for Max). So Min() gives oo and Max() gives -oo, as the issue asks. This matches what I recall of the upstream fix, but I could not check the repo's current code.
